title.zh: 卷七十九 志第五十五 食貨三
title.raw: 卷七十九 志第五十五 食貨三 Volume 79 Treatises 55: Finance and Economics 3

sentences.zh: 漕運倉庫

translations.literal: Grain Transport Warehouses
translations.idiomatic: Grain Transport and Warehouses

sentences.zh: 歷代以來，漕粟所都，給官府廩食，各視道里遠近以為準。

translations.literal: Throughout the ages, the places where transported grain was stored supplied government granaries for official rations, each according to the distance of the route.
translations.idiomatic: From dynasty to dynasty, grain transported by the canal was stored at relay depots to supply government granaries, with provisions scaled to the distance of each leg of the route.

sentences.zh: 太祖都金陵，四方貢賦，由江以達京師，道近而易。

translations.literal: When the founding emperor made his capital at Jinling, tribute and taxes from all quarters reached the capital by river, the route being short and easy.
translations.idiomatic: When the Hongwu Emperor established his capital at Nanjing, tribute and taxes from every region reached the capital by the Yangtze, a route that was short and straightforward.

sentences.zh: 自成祖遷燕，道里遼遠，法凡三變。

translations.literal: From the time the Yongle Emperor moved to Yan, the distance was vast and remote, and the regulations changed three times in all.
translations.idiomatic: After the Yongle Emperor moved the capital to Beijing, the haul became vastly longer, and the transport system was reorganized three times.

sentences.zh: 初支運，次兌運、支運相參，至支運悉變為長運而制定。

translations.literal: At first there was relay transport; next exchange transport and relay transport were used together, until relay transport was wholly changed into long-distance transport and the system was fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The system began with relay transport, then combined exchange and relay transport, until relay transport was entirely replaced by long-distance transport and the regulations were set in their final form.

sentences.zh: 自浚會通河，帝命都督賈義、尚書宋禮以舟師運。

translations.literal: After the Huitong Canal was dredged, the emperor ordered Regional Commander Jia Yi and Minister Song Li to transport grain by naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Huitong Canal had been dredged, the emperor ordered Regional Commander Jia Yi and Minister Song Li to move grain by fleet.

sentences.zh: 禮以海船大者千石，工窳輒敗，乃造淺船五百艘，運淮、揚、徐、兗糧百萬，以當海運之數。

translations.literal: Li, because sea-going vessels of a thousand piculs were poorly built and often broke up, then built five hundred shallow-draft boats and transported a million piculs of grain from Huai, Yang, Xu, and Yan to match the quota of sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: Song Li found that thousand-picul seagoing ships were shoddily built and kept breaking apart, so he built five hundred shallow-draft boats and moved a million piculs of grain from the Huai, Yang, Xu, and Yan regions to replace the volume formerly carried by sea.

sentences.zh: 平江伯陳瑄繼之，頗增至三千餘艘。

translations.literal: Pingjiang Earl Chen Xuan succeeded him and increased the fleet to more than three thousand vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Pingjiang Earl Chen Xuan took over from him and expanded the fleet to more than three thousand vessels.

sentences.zh: 時淮、徐、臨清、德州各有倉。

translations.literal: At that time Huai, Xu, Linqing, and Dezhou each had warehouses.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were warehouses at Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖廣、浙江民運糧至淮安倉，分遣官軍就近輓運。

translations.literal: The people of Jiangxi, Huguang, and Zhejiang transported grain to the Huai'an warehouse, and government troops were dispatched in sections to haul it from nearby points.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants from Jiangxi, Huguang, and Zhejiang delivered grain to the Huai'an depot, and government troops were assigned in relays to haul it onward from each stage.

sentences.zh: 自淮至徐以浙、直軍，自徐至德以京衛軍，自德至通以山東、河南軍。

translations.literal: From Huai to Xu the troops of Zhejiang and Zhili were used; from Xu to De the capital garrison troops; from De to Tong the troops of Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Troops from Zhejiang and the metropolitan region hauled grain from Huai'an to Xuzhou; capital garrison troops from Xuzhou to Dezhou; and Shandong and Henan troops from Dezhou to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 以次遞運，歲凡四次，可三百萬餘石，名曰支運。

translations.literal: Transport proceeded in relays in order, four times a year in all, amounting to more than three million piculs, and was called relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Grain moved in relays along the route, with four runs each year totaling more than three million piculs; this was called relay transport.

sentences.zh: 支運之法，支者，不必出當年之民納；

translations.literal: In the method of relay transport, those who hauled did not have to draw on the grain the people paid in that same year;
translations.idiomatic: Under relay transport, the troops who hauled grain did not have to draw on the tribute grain the peasants delivered in that same year;

sentences.zh: 納者，不必供當年之軍支。

translations.literal: those who paid in did not have to supply that year's military haul.
translations.idiomatic: and those who delivered grain did not have to supply the haul required of the troops in that same year.

sentences.zh: 通數年以為裒益，期不失常額而止。

translations.literal: Totals over several years were used for gain and loss, with the aim only of not falling short of the regular quota.
translations.idiomatic: Accounts were balanced over several years so that the regular quota was met without requiring exact annual matching.

sentences.zh: 由是海陸二運皆罷，惟存遮洋船，每歲於河南、山東、小灘等水次，兌糧三十萬石，十二輸天津，十八由直沽入海輸薊州而已。

translations.literal: Thereupon both sea and land transport were abolished; only ocean-going escort vessels remained. Each year at landings in Henan, Shandong, Xiaotan, and elsewhere, three hundred thousand piculs of grain were exchanged: twelve-tenths went to Tianjin, eighteen-tenths entered the sea at Zhigu and were delivered to Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sea and overland transport were both discontinued; only escort vessels for coastal runs remained. Each year at landings in Henan, Shandong, Xiaotan, and elsewhere, three hundred thousand piculs were exchanged—one hundred twenty thousand piculs to Tianjin and one hundred eighty thousand piculs shipped from Zhigu by sea to Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 不數年，官軍多所調遣，遂復民運，道遠數愆期。

translations.literal: Within a few years government troops were widely dispatched on other duties, and civilian transport was restored; the routes were long and deadlines were often missed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few years many transport troops were reassigned to other duties, civilian haulage was restored, and because the routes were so long deliveries often missed their deadlines.

sentences.zh: 宣德四年，瑄及尚書黃福建議復支運法，乃令江西、湖廣、浙江民運百五十萬石於淮安倉，蘇、鬆、甯、池、廬、安、廣德民運糧二百七十四萬石於徐州倉，應天、常、鎮、淮、揚、鳳、太、滁、和、徐民運糧二百二十萬石於臨清倉，令官軍接運入京、通二倉。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xuande, Xuan and Minister Huang Fu jointly proposed restoring relay transport. They ordered the people of Jiangxi, Huguang, and Zhejiang to transport 1.5 million piculs to the Huai'an warehouse; the people of Su, Song, Ning, Chi, Lu, An, and Guangde to transport 2.74 million piculs to the Xuzhou warehouse; and the people of Yingtian, Chang, Zhen, Huai, Yang, Feng, Tai, Chu, He, and Xu to transport 2.2 million piculs to the Linqing warehouse, with government troops to take over and deliver into the Beijing and Tongzhou warehouses.
translations.idiomatic: In Xuande 4, Chen Xuan and Minister Huang Fu jointly proposed restoring relay transport. Peasants from Jiangxi, Huguang, and Zhejiang were to deliver 1.5 million piculs to Huai'an; those from Suzhou, Songjiang, Ningguo, Chizhou, Luzhou, Anqing, and Guangde 2.74 million piculs to Xuzhou; and those from Yingtian, Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, Fengyang, Taiping, Chuzhou, Hezhou, and Xuzhou 2.2 million piculs to Linqing, with transport troops relaying the grain into the Beijing and Tongzhou depots.

sentences.zh: 民糧既就近入倉，力大減省，乃量地近遠，糧多寡，抽民船十一或十三、五之一以給官軍。

translations.literal: Once the people's grain was stored in nearby warehouses, labor was greatly reduced. They then measured distance and amount of grain and took one-eleventh or one-thirteenth or one-fifteenth of civilian boats to supply the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Because peasants now delivered grain to nearby depots, their labor was greatly reduced. The state then assessed distance and volume and requisitioned one boat in eleven, thirteen, or fifteen from civilian fleets to supply the transport troops.

sentences.zh: 惟山東、河南、北直隸則徑赴京倉，不用支運。

translations.literal: Only Shandong, Henan, and North Zhili went directly to the capital warehouses and did not use relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Only Shandong, Henan, and North Zhili delivered grain straight to the capital depots without relay transport.

sentences.zh: 尋令南陽、懷慶、汝寧糧運臨清倉，開封、彰德、衛輝糧運德州倉，其後山東、河南皆運德州倉。

translations.literal: Soon Nanyang, Huaqing, and Runing grain was sent to the Linqing warehouse; Kaifeng, Zhangde, and Weihui grain to the Dezhou warehouse; thereafter all Shandong and Henan grain went to the Dezhou warehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward grain from Nanyang, Huaqing, and Runing was routed to Linqing; grain from Kaifeng, Zhangde, and Weihui to Dezhou; and eventually all Shandong and Henan grain went to Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 六年，瑄言：「江南民運糧諸倉，往返幾一年，誤農業。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Xuan said: "When the people of Jiangnan transport grain to the various warehouses, the round trip takes nearly a year and disrupts agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Chen Xuan said: "When Jiangnan peasants haul grain to the various depots, the round trip takes nearly a year and ruins the farming season.

sentences.zh: 令民運至淮安、瓜洲，兌與衛所。

translations.literal: Let the people transport only as far as Huai'an and Guazhou and exchange the grain with the guard units.
translations.idiomatic: Let peasants deliver only as far as Huai'an and Guazhou and hand the grain over to the guard units there.

sentences.zh: 官軍運載至北，給與路費耗米，則軍民兩便。」

translations.literal: Government troops will carry it north and be given travel expenses and surplus grain, and both military and civilians will benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Government troops will carry it north in return for travel expenses and surplus allowances, benefiting both soldiers and civilians."

sentences.zh: 是為兌運。

translations.literal: This was called exchange transport.
translations.idiomatic: This became known as exchange transport.

sentences.zh: 命羣臣會議。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the ministers to confer.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered a council of ministers.

sentences.zh: 吏部蹇義等上官軍兌運民糧加耗則例，以地遠近為差。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Personnel, Jian Yi and others, submitted regulations for surplus allowances when government troops exchanged transport for civilian grain, graded by distance.
translations.idiomatic: Jian Yi of the Ministry of Personnel and others submitted graded surplus-allowance rates for grain that troops exchanged from civilians, scaled by distance.

sentences.zh: 每石，湖廣八斗，江西、浙江七斗，南直隸六斗，北直隸五斗。

translations.literal: Per picul: Huguang eight dou, Jiangxi and Zhejiang seven dou, South Zhili six dou, North Zhili five dou.
translations.idiomatic: Per picul the allowance was eight dou for Huguang, seven for Jiangxi and Zhejiang, six for South Zhili, and five for North Zhili.

sentences.zh: 民有運至淮安兌與軍運者，止加四斗，如有兌運不盡，仍令民自運赴諸倉，不願兌者，亦聽其自運。

translations.literal: For civilians who transported to Huai'an and exchanged with military transport, only four dou were added. If exchange transport was not completed, the people were still ordered to transport themselves to the various warehouses; those unwilling to exchange were also permitted to transport on their own.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants who delivered to Huai'an and exchanged with transport troops received only a four-dou surplus. Any grain not covered by exchange was still hauled by civilians to the depots, and those who declined to exchange could continue hauling on their own.

sentences.zh: 軍既加耗，又給輕齎銀為洪閘盤撥之費，且得附載他物，皆樂從事，而民亦多以遠運為艱。

translations.literal: The troops, having surplus allowances and also receiving light-cargo silver for lock and transshipment expenses, and being allowed to carry other goods as well, all gladly took the work, while the people also found long-distance transport hard.
translations.idiomatic: Troops welcomed the work because they received surplus grain, light-cargo silver for locks and transshipment, and permission to carry other goods on the side, while civilians increasingly found long-distance hauling burdensome.

sentences.zh: 於是兌運者多，而支運者少矣。

translations.literal: Thus exchange transport became more common and relay transport less.
translations.idiomatic: Exchange transport therefore grew common while relay transport declined.

sentences.zh: 軍與民兌米，往往恃強勒索。

translations.literal: When troops and civilians exchanged grain, the troops often relied on force to extort.
translations.idiomatic: When troops exchanged grain with civilians, they often used their power to extort extra payments.

sentences.zh: 帝知其弊，敕戶部委正官監臨，不許私兌。

translations.literal: The emperor knew this abuse and ordered the Ministry of Revenue to dispatch proper officials to supervise and forbid private exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Aware of the abuse, the emperor ordered the Ministry of Revenue to send supervising officials and forbid private exchanges.

sentences.zh: 已而頗減加耗米，遠者不過六斗，近者至二斗五升。

translations.literal: Later surplus grain was considerably reduced: for distant routes no more than six dou, for near routes down to two dou five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus allowances were later cut substantially—to six dou at most for distant routes and as little as two dou five sheng for nearby ones.

sentences.zh: 以三分為率，二分與米，一分以他物準。

translations.literal: Taking three parts as the rate, two parts were given in grain and one part was commuted in other goods.
translations.idiomatic: Of each allowance, two-thirds was paid in grain and one-third commuted in other goods.

sentences.zh: 正糧斛面銳，耗糧俱平概。

translations.literal: For principal grain the measure was heaped; for surplus grain all was leveled.
translations.idiomatic: Principal grain was measured heaped in the bushel, while surplus grain was measured level.

sentences.zh: 運糧四百萬石，京倉貯十四，通倉貯十六。

translations.literal: Of four million piculs transported, fourteen parts were stored in the capital warehouse and sixteen in the Tong warehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Of the four million piculs transported, fourteen parts went to the capital depot and sixteen to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 臨、徐、淮三倉各遣御史監收。

translations.literal: To the Linqing, Xu, and Huai warehouses censors were each dispatched to supervise collection.
translations.idiomatic: Censors were assigned to supervise receipts at the Linqing, Xuzhou, and Huai'an depots.

sentences.zh: 正統初，運糧之數四百五十萬石，而兌運者二百八十萬餘石，淮、徐、臨、德四倉支運者十之三四耳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhengtong the transport quota was 4.5 million piculs; of this more than 2.8 million were by exchange transport, while relay transport through the four warehouses of Huai, Xu, Linqing, and De accounted for only three or four tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhengtong reign the transport quota was 4.5 million piculs, of which more than 2.8 million moved by exchange transport; relay hauls through Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou made up only three or four tenths.

sentences.zh: 土木之變，復盡留山東、直隸軍操備。

translations.literal: After the Tumu crisis, Shandong and Zhili troops were again all kept for drill and readiness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Tumu debacle, Shandong and Zhili transport troops were again kept entirely for training and defense.

sentences.zh: 蘇、鬆諸府運糧仍屬民。

translations.literal: Grain transport in Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures again fell to the people.
translations.idiomatic: Grain hauling in Suzhou, Songjiang, and neighboring prefectures again fell to civilians.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年，瓦剌入貢，乃復軍運。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Jingtai the Oirats came to pay tribute, and military transport was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingtai 6, after the Oirats sent tribute missions, military transport was restored.

sentences.zh: 天順末，兌運法行久，倉入覬耗餘，入庾率兌斛面，且求多索，軍困甚。

translations.literal: Late in Tianshun, exchange transport having been in force long, warehouse clerks coveted surplus grain; grain entered the granary mostly by exchange measure heaped, and they demanded extra levies, so the troops were greatly distressed.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Tianshun reign, after exchange transport had been in place for years, warehouse clerks coveted surplus allowances, routinely measured incoming grain by the heaped exchange bushel, and demanded extra levies, leaving transport troops in severe distress.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，漕運參將袁佑上言便宜。

translations.literal: When the Xianzong Emperor took the throne, Grain Transport Assistant Commander Yuan You submitted proposals for convenience.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xianzong acceded, Assistant Commander Yuan You of the grain transport service submitted practical reforms.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「律令明言，收糧令納戶平準，石加耗不過五升。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The statutes clearly state that in collecting grain the delivering household is to level the measure, and surplus per picul must not exceed five sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "The statutes clearly require delivering households to level the measure themselves, and surplus allowances must not exceed five sheng per picul.

sentences.zh: 今運軍願明加，則倉吏侵害過多可知。

translations.literal: Now that transport troops ask for open surplus allowances, it is clear that warehouse clerks have been overreaching in their exactions.
translations.idiomatic: That transport troops now plead for open surplus allowances shows how badly warehouse clerks have been overcharging them.

sentences.zh: 今後令軍自概，每石加耗五升，毋溢，勒索者治罪。」

translations.literal: Henceforth let the troops level the measure themselves, with five sheng surplus per picul and no excess; those who extort shall be punished."
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth troops shall level the measure themselves, with five sheng surplus per picul and no more; extortionists will be punished."

sentences.zh: 後從督倉中官言，加耗至八升。

translations.literal: Later, following the eunuch supervisors of the warehouses, surplus was raised to eight sheng.
translations.idiomatic: Later, at the urging of the eunuchs who supervised the depots, the surplus allowance was raised to eight sheng.

sentences.zh: 久之，復溢收如故，屢禁不能止也。

translations.literal: After a long time over-collection resumed as before; repeated prohibitions could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long over-collection resumed as before, and repeated prohibitions failed to stop it.

sentences.zh: 初，運糧京師，未有定額。

translations.literal: At first grain transport to the capital had no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Initially grain shipments to the capital had no fixed quota.

sentences.zh: 成化八年始定四百萬石，自後以為常。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chenghua four million piculs was first fixed, and thereafter taken as the regular amount.
translations.idiomatic: In Chenghua 8 the quota was fixed at four million piculs and thereafter treated as the standard.

sentences.zh: 北糧七十五萬五千六百石，南糧三百二十四萬四千四百石，其內兌運者三百三十萬石，由支運改兌者七十萬石。

translations.literal: Northern grain was 755,600 piculs, southern grain 3,244,400 piculs; within this, exchange transport was 3.3 million piculs, and grain converted from relay to exchange was 700,000 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Northern grain totaled 755,600 piculs and southern grain 3,244,400 piculs; of this, 3.3 million piculs moved by exchange transport and 700,000 piculs were converted from relay to exchange.

sentences.zh: 兌運之中，湖廣、山東、河南折色十七萬七千七百石。

translations.literal: Within exchange transport, Huguang, Shandong, and Henan commuted 177,700 piculs to silver.
translations.idiomatic: Of the exchange transport total, Huguang, Shandong, and Henan commuted 177,700 piculs to silver payments.

sentences.zh: 通計兌運、改兌加以耗米入京、通兩倉者，凡五百十八萬九千七百石。

translations.literal: Altogether, exchange transport, converted exchange, and surplus grain entering the Beijing and Tong warehouses totaled 5,189,700 piculs.
translations.idiomatic: Counting exchange transport, converted exchange, and surplus grain together, 5,189,700 piculs entered the Beijing and Tongzhou depots.

sentences.zh: 而南直隸正糧獨百八十萬，薊州一府七十萬，加耗在外。

translations.literal: South Zhili alone contributed 1.8 million piculs of principal grain; Jizhou prefecture alone seventy thousand, surplus allowances apart.
translations.idiomatic: South Zhili alone supplied 1.8 million piculs of principal grain and Jizhou prefecture seventy thousand, not counting surplus allowances.

sentences.zh: 浙賦視蘇減數萬。

translations.literal: Zhejiang's levy was tens of thousands less than Suzhou's.
translations.idiomatic: Zhejiang's tax quota was tens of thousands of piculs below Suzhou's.

sentences.zh: 江西、湖廣又殺焉。

translations.literal: Jiangxi and Huguang were reduced still further.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi and Huguang were lower still.

sentences.zh: 天津、蘇州、密雲、昌平，共給米六十四萬餘石，悉支兌運米。

translations.literal: Tianjin, Suzhou, Miyun, and Changping together were supplied more than 640,000 piculs of grain, all drawn from exchange-transport grain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjin, Suzhou, Miyun, and Changping together received more than 640,000 piculs, all drawn from exchange-transport stocks.

sentences.zh: 而臨、德二倉，貯預備米十九萬餘石，取山東、河南改兌米充之。

translations.literal: The Linqing and De warehouses stored more than 190,000 piculs of reserve grain, filled with converted-exchange grain from Shandong and Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Linqing and Dezhou depots held more than 190,000 piculs of reserve grain, supplied from converted-exchange grain in Shandong and Henan.

sentences.zh: 遇災傷，則撥二倉米以補運，務足四百萬之額，不令缺也。

translations.literal: When disaster or crop failure occurred, grain from the two warehouses was allocated to supplement transport, striving to make up the four-million quota and not allow a shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: After disasters or crop failures, grain from the two depots was drawn to keep transport at the four-million-picul quota without shortfall.

sentences.zh: 至成化七年，乃有改兌之議。

translations.literal: By the seventh year of Chenghua there arose the proposal for converted exchange.
translations.idiomatic: By Chenghua 7 the proposal for converted exchange had emerged.

sentences.zh: 時應天巡撫滕昭令運軍赴江南水次交兌，加耗外，復石增米一斗為渡江費。

translations.literal: At that time Yingtian Grand Coordinator Teng Zhao ordered transport troops to go to Jiangnan landings for exchange; beyond surplus allowances, one dou per picul was again added as a Yangtze crossing fee.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yingtian Grand Coordinator Teng Zhao ordered transport troops to collect grain at Jiangnan landings; beyond surplus allowances, they added one dou per picul as a Yangtze crossing fee.

sentences.zh: 後數年，帝乃命淮、徐、臨、德四倉支運七十萬石之米，悉改水次交兌。

translations.literal: Several years later the emperor ordered the seven hundred thousand piculs of relay transport through the four warehouses of Huai, Xu, Linqing, and De all to be changed to exchange at landings.
translations.idiomatic: Several years later the emperor ordered the seven hundred thousand piculs hauled by relay through Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou all converted to landing-side exchange.

sentences.zh: 由是悉變為改兌，而官軍長運遂為定制。

translations.literal: Thereby all became converted exchange, and long-distance transport by government troops was fixed as the established system.
translations.idiomatic: Everything was thereby converted to landing-side exchange, and long-distance haulage by government troops became the permanent system.

sentences.zh: 然是時，司倉者多苛取，甚至有額外罰，運軍輾轉稱貸不支。

translations.literal: Yet at this time warehouse officials mostly exacted harshly, and there were even extra fines; transport troops turned repeatedly to borrowing and could not meet payments.
translations.idiomatic: Yet warehouse officials mostly exacted harsh fees, sometimes imposing extra fines, and transport troops borrowed repeatedly and still could not pay.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年，都御史馬文升疏論運軍之苦，言：「各直省運船，皆工部給價，令有司監造。

translations.literal: In the first year of Hongzhi Censor-in-Chief Ma Wensheng memorialized on the hardships of transport troops, saying: "Transport vessels of each province are all priced by the Ministry of Works and ordered built under local supervision.
translations.idiomatic: In Hongzhi 1, Censor-in-Chief Ma Wensheng memorialized on the transport troops' hardships, saying: "Transport vessels in every province are priced by the Ministry of Works and built under local supervision.

sentences.zh: 近者，漕運總兵以價不時給，請領價自造。

translations.literal: Recently the grain-transport commander-in-chief, because prices were not paid on time, asked to receive the funds and build the boats himself.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the grain-transport commander, because funds were not paid on schedule, asked to receive the money and build the boats himself.

sentences.zh: 而部臣慮軍士不加愛護，議令本部出料四分，軍衛任三分，舊船抵三分。

translations.literal: But ministry officials feared the soldiers would not care for the boats and proposed that the ministry supply materials for four-tenths, the guard units bear three-tenths, and old boats count for three-tenths.
translations.idiomatic: Ministry officials, fearing troops would not maintain new boats, proposed that the ministry supply materials for four-tenths of the cost, guard units three-tenths, and old boats count for three-tenths.

sentences.zh: 軍衛無從措辦，皆軍士賣資產、鬻男女以供之，以造船之苦也。

translations.literal: The guard units had no means to provide this; all the soldiers sold property and even sold sons and daughters to supply it—such was the hardship of building boats.
translations.idiomatic: Guard units could not raise their share; soldiers sold property and even sold children to pay for it—such was the burden of building transport boats.

sentences.zh: 正軍逃亡數多，而額數不減，俱以餘丁充之，一戶有三、四人應役者。

translations.literal: Many principal soldiers fled, yet the quota did not decrease; all were filled by surplus males, and one household might have three or four men on service.
translations.idiomatic: Many principal soldiers deserted while quotas stayed unchanged, so surplus males filled the rolls and one household might have three or four men on transport duty.

sentences.zh: 春兌秋歸，艱辛萬狀。

translations.literal: Exchange in spring and return in autumn—myriad forms of hardship.
translations.idiomatic: They exchanged grain in spring and returned in autumn, enduring every kind of hardship.

sentences.zh: 船至張家灣，又僱車盤撥，多稱貸以濟用，此往來之苦也。

translations.literal: When boats reached Zhangjiawan they again hired carts for transshipment, often borrowing to make ends meet—such was the hardship of the journey back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhangjiawan they hired carts for transshipment and often borrowed money to cover costs—another hardship of the round trip.

sentences.zh: 其所稱貸，運官因以侵漁，責償倍息。

translations.literal: The loans they took out transport officials then used to prey upon them, demanding repayment at double interest.
translations.idiomatic: Transport officials then preyed on those loans, demanding repayment at double interest.

sentences.zh: 而軍士或自載土產以易薪米，又格於禁例，多被掠奪。

translations.literal: Soldiers who carried local products to trade for fuel and grain were again blocked by prohibitions and often plundered.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers who carried local goods to trade for fuel and grain were blocked by prohibitions and often robbed.

sentences.zh: 今宜加造船費每艘銀二十兩，而禁約運官及有司科害搜檢之弊，庶軍困少蘇。」

translations.literal: Now boat-building costs should be increased by twenty taels of silver per vessel, and transport officials and local offices should be forbidden from levies, harm, and search abuses, so that military hardship may be somewhat relieved."
translations.idiomatic: Boat-building subsidies should be raised by twenty taels of silver per vessel, and transport officials and local offices forbidden from levies, harassment, and abusive searches, so troops might gain some relief."

sentences.zh: 詔從其議。

translations.literal: An edict approved his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 五年，戶部尚書葉淇言：「蘇、鬆諸府，連歲荒歉，民買漕米，每石銀二兩。

translations.literal: In the fifth year Minister of Revenue Ye Qi said: "In Suzhou, Songjiang, and other prefectures, years of famine in succession—when the people buy transport grain, each picul costs two taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Minister Ye Qi said: "Suzhou, Songjiang, and neighboring prefectures have suffered successive crop failures; peasants who buy transport grain pay two taels of silver per picul.

sentences.zh: 而北直隸、山東、河南歲供宣、大二邊糧料，每石亦銀一兩。

translations.literal: North Zhili, Shandong, and Henan each year supply grain and fodder to the Xuan and Da border regions, also one tael of silver per picul.
translations.idiomatic: North Zhili, Shandong, and Henan annually supply grain and fodder to the Xuan and Da frontier zones at one tael of silver per picul as well.

sentences.zh: 去歲，蘇州兌運已折五十萬石，每石銀一兩。

translations.literal: Last year Suzhou exchange transport already commuted five hundred thousand piculs at one tael of silver per picul.
translations.idiomatic: Last year Suzhou already commuted five hundred thousand piculs of exchange transport at one tael per picul.

sentences.zh: 今請推行於諸府，而稍差其直。

translations.literal: Now I ask to extend this to all prefectures, with slight variation in price.
translations.idiomatic: I propose extending this to all prefectures with slightly varied rates.

sentences.zh: 災重者，石七錢，稍輕者，石仍一兩。

translations.literal: Where disaster was severe, seven qian per picul; where lighter, still one tael per picul.
translations.idiomatic: Where disaster was severe, seven qian per picul; where lighter, one tael per picul.

sentences.zh: 俱解部轉發各邊，抵北直隸三處歲供之數，而收三處本色以輸京倉，則費省而事易集。」

translations.literal: All would be remitted to the ministry and forwarded to the border regions, offsetting the annual supply from the three North Zhili places, while collecting grain in kind from those three places to deliver to the capital warehouse—thus costs would be saved and the matter easily accomplished."
translations.idiomatic: Silver would go to the ministry for forwarding to the frontiers, offsetting the annual grain supply from the three North Zhili regions, while those regions paid grain in kind to the capital depot—saving expense and simplifying collection."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 自後歲災，輒權宜折銀，以水次倉支運之糧充其數，而折價以六七錢為率，無復至一兩者。

translations.literal: Thereafter, in years of disaster, silver commutation was used as expedient; grain from landing warehouses for relay transport made up the quota, and commutation prices mostly ran six or seven qian, no longer reaching one tael.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward, in famine years the state routinely commuted grain to silver, filling quotas with relay grain from landing depots at rates of six or seven qian per picul, never again reaching one tael.

sentences.zh: 先是，成化間行長運之法。

translations.literal: Earlier, during Chenghua, the method of long-distance transport was implemented.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, during the Chenghua reign, long-distance transport had been introduced.

sentences.zh: 江南州縣運糧至南京，令官軍就水次兌支，計省加耗輸輓之費，得餘米十萬石有奇，貯預備倉以資緩急之用。

translations.literal: Jiangnan prefectures and counties transported grain to Nanjing and ordered government troops to exchange and draw at landings; counting savings in surplus, hauling, and relay costs, more than a hundred thousand piculs of surplus grain were obtained and stored in reserve warehouses for emergency use.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangnan counties delivered grain to Nanjing and had troops collect it at landings; savings on surplus allowances and relay costs yielded more than a hundred thousand piculs of surplus grain, stored in reserve depots for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 至是，巡撫都御史以兌支有弊，請令如舊上倉而後放支。

translations.literal: At this time the grand coordinator and censor-in-chief, because exchange and draw had abuses, asked that the old practice of entering the warehouse first and then releasing grain be restored.
translations.idiomatic: The grand coordinator then argued that landing-side exchange was prone to abuse and asked to restore the old rule of storing grain in the warehouse before release.

sentences.zh: 戶部言：「兌支法善，不可易。」

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue said: "The method of exchange and draw is good and must not be changed."
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue replied: "Landing-side exchange works well and must not be changed."

sentences.zh: 詔從部議，以所餘就貯各衛倉，作正支銷。

translations.literal: An edict followed the ministry's view; the surplus was stored in each guard warehouse and issued as principal expenditure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sided with the ministry and stored the surplus in guard depots for regular disbursement.

sentences.zh: 又從戶部言，山東改兌糧九萬石，仍聽民自運臨、德二倉，令官軍支運。

translations.literal: Again following the Ministry of Revenue, ninety thousand piculs of Shandong converted-exchange grain were still permitted to be transported by the people themselves to the Linqing and De warehouses, with government troops to relay it.
translations.idiomatic: Following the ministry again, ninety thousand piculs of Shandong converted-exchange grain could still be hauled by civilians to Linqing and Dezhou for relay by transport troops.

sentences.zh: 正德二年，漕運官請疏通水次倉儲，言：「往時民運至淮、徐、臨、德四倉，以待衛軍支運，後改附近州縣水次交兌。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhengde grain-transport officials asked to clear landing warehouses, saying: "Formerly the people transported to the four warehouses of Huai, Xu, Linqing, and De to await relay by guard troops; later nearby prefectures and counties were changed to exchange at landings.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengde 2 grain-transport officials proposed clearing landing depots, noting: "Peasants once delivered to Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou to await guard relay hauls, but nearby counties were later switched to landing-side exchange.

sentences.zh: 已而並支運七十萬石亦令改兌。

translations.literal: Then the seven hundred thousand piculs of relay transport were also ordered converted to exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Then the seven hundred thousand piculs of relay transport were also ordered converted to exchange.

sentences.zh: 但七十萬石之外，猶有交兌不盡者，民仍運赴四倉，久無支銷，以致陳腐。

translations.literal: Beyond the seven hundred thousand piculs, there was still grain not fully exchanged; the people still transported to the four warehouses, which long went without disbursement and thus spoiled.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond those seven hundred thousand piculs, grain still not exchanged at landings was hauled to the four depots, where it sat undisbursed until it spoiled.

sentences.zh: 請將浙江、江西、湖廣正兌糧米三十五萬石，折銀解京，而令三省衛軍赴臨、德等倉，支運如所折之數。

translations.literal: They asked that three hundred fifty thousand piculs of principal exchange grain from Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Huguang be commuted to silver and sent to the capital, while guard troops of the three provinces went to the Linqing and De warehouses to relay transport in the amount commuted.
translations.idiomatic: They proposed commuting three hundred fifty thousand piculs of principal exchange grain from Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Huguang to silver for Beijing, while guard troops from those provinces relayed an equal volume from Linqing and Dezhou.

sentences.zh: 則諸倉米不腐，三省漕卒便於支運。

translations.literal: Then grain in the various warehouses would not spoil, and transport troops of the three provinces would find relay transport convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Depot grain would not spoil, and transport troops from the three provinces could relay hauls more easily.

sentences.zh: 歲漕額外，又得三十五萬折銀，一舉而數善具矣。」

translations.literal: Beyond the annual transport quota, another three hundred fifty thousand piculs would be commuted to silver—several benefits achieved at once."
translations.idiomatic: Beyond the annual quota, another three hundred fifty thousand piculs would be commuted to silver—several benefits in one stroke."

sentences.zh: 帝命部臣議，如其請。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered ministry officials to deliberate and granted the request.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the ministries to deliberate and approved the request.

sentences.zh: 六年，戶部侍郎邵寶以漕運遲滯，請復支運法。

translations.literal: In the sixth year Vice Minister of Revenue Shao Bao, because grain transport was delayed, asked to restore relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year Vice Minister Shao Bao, citing transport delays, asked to restore relay transport.

sentences.zh: 戶部議，支運法廢久，不可卒復，事遂寢。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue deliberated that relay transport had long been abandoned and could not be suddenly restored; the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry ruled that relay transport had been abandoned too long to restore abruptly, and the proposal lapsed.

sentences.zh: 臨、德二倉之貯米也，凡十九萬，計十年得百九十萬。

translations.literal: The grain stored in the Linqing and De warehouses totaled one hundred ninety thousand piculs; over ten years this would reach one million nine hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The Linqing and Dezhou depots held one hundred ninety thousand piculs; over ten years that would reach one million nine hundred thousand.

sentences.zh: 自世宗初，災傷撥補日多，而山東、河南以歲歉，數請輕減，且二倉囤積多朽腐。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the Jiajing reign, disaster-relief allocations and make-up payments grew daily; Shandong and Henan, because of poor harvests, repeatedly asked for reductions, and grain heaped in the two depots mostly rotted.
translations.idiomatic: From the start of the Jiajing reign, disaster-relief allocations mounted, and Shandong and Henan—repeatedly hit by bad harvests—kept requesting lighter quotas; meanwhile much of the grain stored in the two warehouses was rotting away.

sentences.zh: 於是改折之議屢興，而倉儲漸耗矣。

translations.literal: Thus proposals for silver commutation frequently arose, and granary stocks gradually dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Proposals to commute grain payments to silver came up again and again, and depot stocks steadily shrank.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年，漕運總兵楊宏，請以輕齎銀聽運官道支，為顧僦舟車之費，不必裝鞘印封，計算羨餘，以苦漕卒。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 1, Grain Transport Commander-in-Chief Yang Hong asked that light-cargo silver be left to transport officers to disburse en route, to cover boat- and cart-hire costs, without needing sealed packets; by calculating surplus allowances, it would burden grain transport troops.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing 1, grain transport commander Yang Hong proposed letting transport officers disburse light-cargo silver along the route for hiring boats and carts, without sealed packets or formal accounting of surplus allowances—a move meant to squeeze grain transport troops.

sentences.zh: 給事、御史交駁之。

translations.literal: Supervising secretaries and censorial officials jointly rebutted it.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretaries and censorial officials joined in opposing the proposal.

sentences.zh: 戶部言：「科道官之論，主於防奸，是也。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue said: "The censorate officials' argument, aimed chiefly at preventing fraud, is correct.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue replied: "The censorate's focus on preventing fraud is right.

sentences.zh: 但輕齎本資轉般費，今慮官軍侵耗，盡取其贏餘以歸太倉，則以腳價為正糧，非立法初意也。」

translations.literal: But light-cargo silver was originally meant to fund relay transport costs; now, fearing encroachment and waste by government troops, taking all surplus allowances for the Taicang Depot would turn hauling fees into principal grain, contrary to the law's original intent."
translations.idiomatic: But light-cargo silver was meant to cover relay transport costs; if officials, fearing waste by grain transport troops, seized every surplus allowance for the Taicang Depot, hauling fees would effectively become principal grain—far from what the law intended."

sentences.zh: 乃議運船至通州，巡倉御史核驗，酌量支用實數，著為定規。

translations.literal: It was then proposed that when transport ships reached Tongzhou, the depot-inspecting censor should verify accounts, disburse actual amounts as appropriate, and fix this as a standing regulation.
translations.idiomatic: They then proposed that at Tongzhou, depot inspectors would verify disbursements, pay out only what was actually needed, and fix the rule permanently.

sentences.zh: 有羨餘，不輸太倉，即用以修船，官旗漁蠹者重罪。

translations.literal: Any surplus allowance would not go to Taicang but be used to repair boats; officials and bannermen who profiteered would be severely punished.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus allowances would stay out of Taicang and go toward boat repairs instead, with heavy penalties for officials and bannermen caught profiteering.

sentences.zh: 輕齎銀者，憲宗以諸倉改兌，給路費，始各有耗米；

translations.literal: As for light-cargo silver: when the Chenghua emperor converted exchanges at the various warehouses, travel expenses were granted, and each shipment first had its own loss allowance;
translations.idiomatic: Light-cargo silver dated from the Chenghua reign, when converted exchange at the warehouses introduced travel allowances and loss grain for each shipment;

sentences.zh: 兌運米，俱一平一銳，故有銳米；

translations.literal: Exchange transport grain all used one level and one heaped measure, hence there was heaped grain;
translations.idiomatic: Exchange-transport grain was measured both level and heaped, creating the so-called heaped surplus;

sentences.zh: 自隨船給運四斗外，餘折銀，謂之輕齎。

translations.literal: Beyond four dou given per shi with the boat shipment, the remainder was commuted to silver, called light-cargo silver.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond four dou allotted per shi aboard each vessel, the rest was commuted to silver—this was light-cargo silver.

sentences.zh: 凡四十四萬五千餘兩。

translations.literal: In all, more than 445,000 taels.
translations.idiomatic: The total came to more than 445,000 taels.

sentences.zh: 後頗入太倉矣。

translations.literal: Later much of it went into Taicang after all.
translations.idiomatic: In time, much of it was diverted into Taicang anyway.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，運道艱阻，議者欲開膠萊河，復海運。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign, because the transport route was difficult, proponents wanted to open the Jiao-Lai Canal and restore sea transport.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longqing reign, transport conditions worsened, and some officials proposed reopening the Jiao-Lai Canal to revive sea transport.

sentences.zh: 由淮安清江浦口，曆新壩、馬家壕至海倉口，徑抵直沽，止循海套，不泛大洋。

translations.literal: From Huai'an's Qingjiangpu mouth, passing Xingba and Majiahao to Haicang mouth, it would go straight to Zhigu, keeping only to coastal inlets and not crossing the open sea.
translations.idiomatic: The route would run from Huai'an's Qingjiangpu, through Xingba and Majiahao to Haicang, then straight to Zhigu along sheltered coastal waters rather than the open ocean.

sentences.zh: 疏上，遣官勘報，以水多沙磧而止。

translations.literal: When the memorial reached court, officials were sent to investigate; it was stopped because of excess water and sandy shoals.
translations.idiomatic: After the memorial reached court, surveyors reported too much water and sandy shoals, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，漕運總督舒應龍言：「國家兩都並建，淮、徐、臨、德，實南北咽喉。

translations.literal: In the Wanli reign, Grand Coordinator of Grain Transport Shu Yinglong said: "The state maintains two capitals; Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou are truly the north-south throat.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wanli reign, grain transport grand coordinator Shu Yinglong wrote: "With two capitals, Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou are the vital junction between north and south.

sentences.zh: 自兌運久行，臨、德尚有歲積，而淮、徐二倉無粒米。

translations.literal: Since exchange transport had long been in force, Linqing and De still had yearly accumulations, while the Huai and Xu depots had not a grain of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Exchange transport had long been standard: Linqing and Dezhou still accumulated grain each year, but the Huai'an and Xuzhou depots stood empty.

sentences.zh: 請自今山東、河南全熟時，盡徵本色上倉。

translations.literal: He asked that from now on, when Shandong and Henan had full harvests, all grain in kind be levied into the depots.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that whenever Shandong and Henan enjoyed full harvests, grain in kind should be collected in full and delivered to the warehouses.

sentences.zh: 計臨、德已足五十餘萬，則令納於二倉，亦積五十萬石而止。」

translations.literal: When Linqing and De already had more than five hundred thousand, then collection at the two depots should also stop at five hundred thousand shi."
translations.idiomatic: Once Linqing and De held more than five hundred thousand shi, deliveries to the Huai and Xu depots should likewise be capped at five hundred thousand shi."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: Approval was given.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 當是時，折銀漸多。

translations.literal: At that time, silver commutation gradually increased.
translations.idiomatic: By then, more and more grain was being commuted to silver.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三十年，漕運抵京，僅百三十八萬餘石。

translations.literal: In Wanli 30, grain transport reaching the capital was only a little more than 1.38 million shi.
translations.idiomatic: In Wanli 30, only about 1.38 million shi of transport grain reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 而撫臣議載留漕米以濟河工，倉場侍郎趙世卿爭之，言：「太倉入不當出，計二年後，六軍萬姓將待新漕舉炊，倘輸納愆期，不復有京師矣。」

translations.literal: But the grand coordinator proposed keeping loaded transport grain to fund river works; Depot Vice Minister Zhao Shiqing objected, saying: "What enters Taicang should not leave; in two years the armies and populace will depend on new transport grain for cooking; if delivery is late, there will no longer be a capital."
translations.idiomatic: A grand coordinator then proposed diverting loaded transport grain to river works, but Depot Vice Minister Zhao Shiqing protested: "Grain must not leave Taicang once it arrives; in two years the armies and the people will be waiting on the next transport to eat, and if delivery slips, Beijing itself will be gone."

sentences.zh: 蓋災傷折銀，本折漕糧以抵京軍月俸。

translations.literal: For disaster-relief silver commutation was originally meant to commute transport grain to cover the capital garrisons' monthly rations.
translations.idiomatic: Silver commutation for disaster years was originally meant to replace transport grain that paid the capital garrisons' monthly rations.

sentences.zh: 其時混支以給邊餉，遂致銀米兩空，故世卿爭之。

translations.literal: At that time mixed disbursement was used to pay frontier supplies, causing both silver and grain to run out, which is why Shiqing objected.
translations.idiomatic: Instead the funds were being mixed into frontier pay, draining both silver and grain—hence Shiqing's protest.

sentences.zh: 自後倉儲漸匱，漕政亦益馳。

translations.literal: Afterward granary stocks gradually depleted, and transport administration grew laxer still.
translations.idiomatic: Depot stocks kept shrinking after that, and transport administration grew ever laxer.

sentences.zh: 迨於啟、禎，天下蕭然煩費，歲供愈不足支矣。

translations.literal: By the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns, the realm was bleak with mounting expenses, and yearly supplies grew ever harder to meet.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianqi and Chongzhen reigns, the empire was drained by rising costs and annual supplies could barely be met.

sentences.zh: 運船之數，永樂至景泰，大小無定，為數至多。

translations.literal: As for the number of transport boats, from Yongle to Jingtai large and small had no fixed count and were at their greatest.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongle through Jingtai, transport fleets had no fixed size and reached their peak.

sentences.zh: 天順以後，定船萬一千七百七十，官軍十二萬人。

translations.literal: After Tianshun, boats were fixed at 11,770 and government troops at 120,000.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianshun the fleet was fixed at 11,770 vessels crewed by 120,000 government troops.

sentences.zh: 許令附載土宜，免徵稅鈔。

translations.literal: They were permitted to carry local goods on the side, exempt from tax certificates.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were allowed to carry local goods as side cargo, tax-free.

sentences.zh: 孝宗時限十石，神宗時至六十石。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign the limit was ten shi; in the Wanli reign it reached sixty shi.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi capped side cargo at ten shi; by Wanli the limit had risen to sixty.

sentences.zh: 憲宗立運船至京期限，北直隸、河南、山東五月初一日，南直隸七月初一日，其過江支兌者，展一月，浙江、江西、湖廣九月初一日。

translations.literal: The Chenghua emperor set deadlines for transport boats reaching the capital: North Zhili, Henan, and Shandong the first day of the fifth month; South Zhili the first day of the seventh month; those crossing the river for branch exchange received one month extra; Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Huguang the first day of the ninth month.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua set arrival deadlines: North Zhili, Henan, and Shandong by the first day of the fifth month; South Zhili by the seventh month; Yangtze-crossing branch exchange one month later; Zhejiang, Jiangxi, and Huguang by the ninth month.

sentences.zh: 通計三年考成，違限者，運官降罰。

translations.literal: Performance was assessed over three-year cycles; transport officers who missed deadlines were demoted or fined.
translations.idiomatic: Performance was judged on three-year cycles, and officers who missed deadlines faced demotion or fines.

sentences.zh: 武宗列水程圖格，按日次填行止站地，違限之米，頓德州諸倉，曰寄囤。

translations.literal: The Zhengde emperor drew up water-route chart forms, filling in daily stopping places; grain missing deadlines was held at Dezhou and other depots, called temporary holding storage.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde introduced route ledgers recording daily stops; late grain was held at Dezhou and other depots as temporary holding storage.

sentences.zh: 世宗定過淮程限，江北十二月者，江南正月，湖廣、浙江、江西三月，神宗時改為二月。

translations.literal: The Jiajing emperor set Huai River passage deadlines: north of the river in the twelfth month, Jiangnan in the first month, Huguang, Zhejiang, and Jiangxi in the third month—changed to the second month in the Wanli reign.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing set Huai crossing deadlines: north-of-the-river fleets by the twelfth month, Jiangnan by the first, Huguang-Zhejiang-Jiangxi by the third (later moved to the second under Wanli).

sentences.zh: 又改至京限五月者，縮一月，七八九月者，遞縮兩月。

translations.literal: Beijing arrival deadlines in the fifth month were shortened by one month; those in the seventh, eighth, and ninth months were shortened by two months in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Capital arrival dates in May were pulled forward one month; July-through-September deadlines were pulled forward two.

sentences.zh: 後又通縮一月。

translations.literal: Later all were shortened by one more month.
translations.idiomatic: Later every deadline was tightened by another month.

sentences.zh: 神宗初，定十月開倉，十一月兌竣，大縣限船到十日，小縣五日。

translations.literal: Early in Wanli it was fixed: open warehouses in the tenth month, finish exchange in the eleventh; large counties allowed ten days after boats arrived, small counties five days.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wanli the schedule was fixed: warehouses opened in the tenth month and exchange finished in the eleventh; large counties had ten days after boats arrived, small counties five.

sentences.zh: 十二月開幫，二月過淮，三月過洪入閘。

translations.literal: Convoys opened in the twelfth month, passed Huai in the second month, and passed Hongze into the locks in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: Convoys launched in the twelfth month, crossed the Huai by the second month, and cleared Hongze into the locks by the third.

sentences.zh: 皆先期以樣米呈戶部，運糧到日，比驗相同乃收。

translations.literal: Sample grain was submitted to the ministry beforehand; when transport grain arrived, it was received only after comparison showed it matched.
translations.idiomatic: Counties sent sample grain to the ministry in advance; incoming shipments were accepted only after matching the sample.

sentences.zh: 凡災傷奏請改折者，毋過七月。

translations.literal: All disaster-relief memorials requesting silver commutation must not be later than the seventh month.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster-relief requests to commute grain to silver could not be filed after the seventh month.

sentences.zh: 題議後期及臨時改題者，立案免覆。

translations.literal: Late submissions and last-minute revised memorials were recorded once and exempt from re-review.
translations.idiomatic: Late or hastily revised memorials were logged once and exempt from further review.

sentences.zh: 漂流者，抵換食米。

translations.literal: For losses from drifting, substitute rice for consumption was provided.
translations.idiomatic: Drift losses were covered with replacement rice from depots.

sentences.zh: 大江漂流為大患，河道為小患；

translations.literal: Drifting on the great river was a major loss; on canals a minor loss;
translations.idiomatic: Losses on the Yangtze counted as major; canal losses as minor;

sentences.zh: 二百石外為大患，二百石內為小患。

translations.literal: Above two hundred shi was major loss, within two hundred shi minor loss.
translations.idiomatic: Losses above two hundred shi were major; two hundred shi or below, minor.

sentences.zh: 小患把總勘報，大患具奏，其後不計多寡，概行奏勘矣。

translations.literal: Minor losses were investigated and reported by squad leaders; major ones were fully memorialized; later, regardless of amount, all were memorialized and investigated.
translations.idiomatic: Squad leaders reported minor losses; major ones went to the throne—until eventually every loss, large or small, required a memorial.

sentences.zh: 初，船用楠杉，下者乃用鬆。

translations.literal: At first boats used nanmu and fir; inferior ones used pine.
translations.idiomatic: Early boats were built of nanmu and fir; cheaper ones of pine.

sentences.zh: 三年小修，六年大修，十年更造。

translations.literal: Minor repair every three years, major repair every six years, complete rebuild every ten years.
translations.idiomatic: They received minor repairs every three years, overhauls every six, and full rebuilds every ten.

sentences.zh: 每船受正耗米四百七十二石。

translations.literal: Each boat loaded 472 shi of principal and loss grain.
translations.idiomatic: Each vessel was rated for 472 shi of principal and allowance grain.

sentences.zh: 其後船數缺少，一船受米七八百石。

translations.literal: Later, with fewer boats, one boat took seven or eight hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: As the fleet shrank, individual boats were loaded with seven or eight hundred shi.

sentences.zh: 附載夾帶日多，所在稽留違限。

translations.literal: Side loads and smuggled cargo grew daily, causing delays and missed deadlines everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: Side cargo and smuggled goods piled up, causing delays and missed deadlines everywhere.

sentences.zh: 一遇河決，即有漂流，官軍因之為奸。

translations.literal: Whenever a breach in the river occurred there was drifting loss, and government troops took advantage to commit fraud.
translations.idiomatic: Every river breach brought drift losses—and opportunities for grain transport troops to cheat.

sentences.zh: 水次折乾，沿途侵盜，妄稱水火，至有鑿船自沉者。

translations.literal: Grain was dried down at landings, pilfered along the route, falsely claimed lost to water or fire, and some even bored holes to sink their boats deliberately.
translations.idiomatic: Troops shaved grain at landing depots, stole along the route, invented flood and fire losses, and some even scuttled their own boats.

sentences.zh: 明初，命武臣督海運，嘗建漕運使，尋罷。

translations.literal: Early in the Ming, military officers were ordered to supervise sea transport; the post of grain transport commissioner was once established but soon abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming put military officers in charge of sea transport and briefly created a grain-transport commissioner post, then abolished it.

sentences.zh: 成祖以後用御史，又用侍郎、都御史催督，郎中、員外分理，主事督兌，其制不一。

translations.literal: After Yongle censors were used, then vice ministers and censors-in-chief to press supervision, section chiefs and vice directors to divide administration, and principal clerks to oversee exchange—the system was not uniform.
translations.idiomatic: After Yongle came censors, then vice ministers and censor-in-chiefs to press the work, section chiefs to divide duties, and principal clerks to supervise exchange—arrangements shifted repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 景泰二年始設漕運總督於淮安，與總兵、參將同理漕事。

translations.literal: In Jingtai 2 the grain transport grand coordinator was first established at Huai'an, sharing grain affairs with the commander-in-chief and vice commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 2 created the grain transport grand coordinator at Huai'an, who shared transport duties with the commander and vice commanders.

sentences.zh: 漕司領十二總，十二萬軍，與京操十二營軍相準。

translations.literal: The transport office commanded twelve squadrons and 120,000 troops, matching the twelve garrison battalions stationed in the capital for drill.
translations.idiomatic: The transport office ran twelve squadrons totaling 120,000 grain transport troops, matching the capital's twelve drill regiments.

sentences.zh: 初，宣宗令運糧總兵官、巡撫、侍郎歲八月赴京，會議明年漕運事宜，及設漕運總督，則並令總督赴京。

translations.literal: At first the Xuande emperor ordered the grain transport commander, grand coordinators, and vice ministers to come to the capital in the eighth month each year to confer on the next year's transport; after creating the grain transport grand coordinator, he was ordered to come as well.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande required the transport commander, grand coordinators, and vice ministers to meet in Beijing each eighth month to plan the next year's transport; once the grand coordinator post existed, he joined them.

sentences.zh: 至萬曆十八年後始免。

translations.literal: This was not waived until after Wanli 18.
translations.idiomatic: The annual Beijing meeting was not dropped until after Wanli 18.

sentences.zh: 凡歲正月，總漕巡揚州，經理瓜、淮過閘。

translations.literal: Every year in the first month the grand coordinator toured Yangzhou and managed passage through Guazhou and Huai'an locks.
translations.idiomatic: Each first month the grand coordinator toured Yangzhou and managed lock passage at Guazhou and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 總兵駐徐、邳，督過洪入閘，同理漕參政管押赴京。

translations.literal: The commander-in-chief was stationed at Xu and Pi, supervising passage through Hongze into the locks; the transport vice commissioner likewise escorted shipments to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The commander held Xu and Pi, supervising Hongze lock passage; the transport vice commissioner escorted convoys toward the capital.

sentences.zh: 攢運則有御史、郎中，押運則有參政，監兌、理刑、管洪、管廠、管閘、管泉、監倉則有主事，清江、衛河有提舉。

translations.literal: Gathering transport had censors and section chiefs; escorting transport had vice commissioners; overseeing exchange, legal affairs, Hongze, shipyards, locks, springs, and depot supervision had principal clerks; Qingjiang and the Wei Canal had superintendents.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and section chiefs handled convoy assembly; vice commissioners escorted shipments; principal clerks oversaw exchange, discipline, Hongze, shipyards, locks, springs, and depots; Qingjiang and the Wei Canal had their own superintendents.

sentences.zh: 兌畢過淮過洪，巡撫、漕司、河道各以職掌奏報。

translations.literal: After exchange was complete and passage over Huai and Hongze, grand coordinators, the transport office, and canal officials each memorialized within their duties.
translations.idiomatic: After exchange and Huai-Hongze passage, grand coordinators, transport officials, and canal officers each reported within their jurisdictions.

sentences.zh: 有司米不備，軍衛船不備，過淮誤期者，責在巡撫。

translations.literal: If local grain was not ready, guard boats were not ready, or Huai passage was late, responsibility lay with the grand coordinator.
translations.idiomatic: Late grain, missing boats, or missed Huai deadlines fell on the grand coordinator.

sentences.zh: 米具船備，不即驗放，非河梗而壓幫停泊，過洪誤期因而漂凍者，責在漕司。

translations.literal: When grain and boats were ready but not promptly inspected and released, or convoys were held back without canal blockage, missing Hongze deadlines and causing drift or freeze losses, responsibility lay with the transport office.
translations.idiomatic: If grain and boats were ready but inspection was delayed, or convoys were held without cause, causing missed Hongze deadlines and drift or freeze losses, the transport office was blamed.

sentences.zh: 船糧依限，河渠淤淺，疏浚無法，閘坐啟閉失時，不得過洪抵灣者，責在河道。

translations.literal: When boats and grain met deadlines but channels silted, dredging failed, or lock keepers opened and closed mistimed so passage to Hongze and the bay was impossible, responsibility lay with canal officials.
translations.idiomatic: If schedules were met but silted channels, failed dredging, or mistimed locks blocked Hongze passage, canal officials bore the blame.

sentences.zh: 明初，於漕政每加優恤，仁、宣禁役漕舟，宥遲運者。

translations.literal: Early Ming repeatedly granted favors to transport administration; Renzong and Xuanzong forbade requisitioning transport boats and pardoned late arrivals.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming showed transport special favor: Renzong and Xuanzong forbade impressing transport boats and pardoned late convoys.

sentences.zh: 英宗時始扣口糧均攤，而運軍不守法度為民害。

translations.literal: In Yingzong's reign ration deductions and shared levies began, and transport troops broke regulations to harm the people.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yingzong ration cuts and shared levies began, and grain transport troops increasingly abused civilians.

sentences.zh: 自後漕政日馳，軍以耗米易私物，道售稽程。

translations.literal: Afterward transport administration grew lax daily; troops traded loss grain for private goods, selling along the route and missing schedules.
translations.idiomatic: Transport discipline kept slipping; grain transport troops traded allowance grain for private goods, peddled along the route, and missed deadlines.

sentences.zh: 比至，反買倉米補納，多不足數。

translations.literal: By arrival they instead bought depot grain to make up delivery, often falling short of quota.
translations.idiomatic: By the time they arrived they had to buy depot grain to make quota, often coming up short.

sentences.zh: 而糧長率攙沙水於米中，河南、山東尤甚，往往蒸濕浥爛不可食。

translations.literal: Grain chiefs routinely mixed sand and water into the rice; Henan and Shandong were especially bad, and grain often steamed, dampened, and rotted until inedible.
translations.idiomatic: Grain chiefs routinely adulterated rice with sand and water—worst in Henan and Shandong—leaving shipments soggy, moldy, and inedible.

sentences.zh: 權要貸運軍銀以罔取利，至請撥關稅給船料以取償。

translations.literal: Powerful men lent silver to transport troops to extort profit, even asking that customs revenue be allocated for boat funds to collect repayment.
translations.idiomatic: Power brokers lent to grain transport troops at usurious rates, even asking customs revenue be earmarked for boat funds they could seize back.

sentences.zh: 漕運把總率由賄得。

translations.literal: Transport squad leaders mostly obtained their posts through bribes.
translations.idiomatic: Transport squad leaders usually bought their posts.

sentences.zh: 倉場額外科取，歲至十四萬。

translations.literal: Depot yards levied extra quotas outside the standard, reaching 140,000 yearly.
translations.idiomatic: Depot officials levied extra exactions totaling 140,000 taels per year.

sentences.zh: 世宗初政，諸弊多釐革，然漂流、違限二弊，日以滋甚。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing's rule many abuses were reformed, yet the two evils of drifting loss and missed deadlines grew worse daily.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing's early reforms cleared many abuses, but drift losses and missed deadlines kept growing worse.

sentences.zh: 中葉以後，益不可究詰矣。

translations.literal: After the mid-reign it became even more beyond investigation.
translations.idiomatic: By mid-dynasty the corruption was beyond remedy.

sentences.zh: 漕糧之外，蘇、鬆、常、嘉、湖五府，輸運內府白熟粳糯米十七萬四十餘石，內折色八千餘石，各府部糙粳米四萬四千餘石，內折色八千八百餘石，令民運。

translations.literal: Beyond transport grain, the five prefectures of Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou delivered 170,040-odd shi of polished long- and short-grain rice to the inner palace, of which 8,000-odd shi were commuted; each prefecture also delivered 44,000-odd shi of coarse rice, of which 8,800-odd shi were commuted—all hauled by civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Apart from canal grain, Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou sent 170,040 shi of polished palace rice (8,000 shi commuted) plus 44,000 shi of coarse rice per prefecture (8,800 shi commuted)—all moved by civilians.

sentences.zh: 謂之白糧船。

translations.literal: These were called white-grain boats.
translations.idiomatic: These were the white-grain convoys.

sentences.zh: 自長運法行，糧皆軍運，而白糧民運如故。

translations.literal: Since long-distance transport took effect, all grain was hauled by troops, but white grain remained civilian haulage as before.
translations.idiomatic: Long-distance transport put canal grain under military haulage, but white grain stayed on civilian transport.

sentences.zh: 穆宗時，陸樹德言：「軍運以充軍儲，民運以充官祿。

translations.literal: In the Longqing reign Lu Shude said: "Military transport fills army stores; civilian transport fills official salaries.
translations.idiomatic: During Longqing, Lu Shude wrote: "Military transport fills army stores; civilian transport pays official salaries.

sentences.zh: 人知軍運之苦，不知民運尤苦也。

translations.literal: People know the hardship of military transport but do not know civilian transport is even harsher.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone knows how hard military transport is; few realize civilian transport is worse.

sentences.zh: 船戶之求索，運軍之欺陵，洪閘之守候，入京入倉，厥弊百出。

translations.literal: Boat owners' exactions, transport troops' bullying, waiting at Hongze locks, entry into the capital and depots—abuses were countless.
translations.idiomatic: Boat owners' shakedowns, troop bullying, waiting at Hongze locks, and entry into Beijing and the depots spawned endless abuses.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，民運尚有保全之家，十年後無不破矣。

translations.literal: Early in Jiajing some households doing civilian transport still kept their livelihood; after ten years none remained unbroken.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jiajing still had civilian haulers who kept their households intact; within a decade every one was ruined.

sentences.zh: 以白糧令軍帶運甚便。」

translations.literal: Having troops carry white grain along with their loads would be very convenient."
translations.idiomatic: Putting white grain on military convoys would be far simpler."

sentences.zh: 疏入，下部議。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it was sent to the ministries for deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the ministries for review.

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: It was not adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was rejected.

sentences.zh: 凡諸倉應輸者有定數，其或改撥他鎮者，水次應兌漕糧，即令坐派鎮軍領兌者給價，州縣官督車戶運至遠倉，或給軍價就令關支者，通謂之穵運。

translations.literal: Each depot had fixed delivery quotas; when grain was reassigned to other garrisons, exchange transport grain at landing depots had the assigned garrison troops who received exchange pay the price; county officials supervised cart contractors to haul to distant depots, or paid troops to draw directly at the gate—all generally called direct-assignment transport.
translations.idiomatic: Each depot owed fixed deliveries; when quotas were shifted to other garrisons, troops assigned to receive exchange grain at landing depots paid the price while county officials sent cart contractors to distant depots—or paid troops to draw at the gate. All this was called direct-assignment transport.

sentences.zh: 九邊之地，輸糧大率以車，宣德時，餉開平亦然，而蘭、甘、松潘，往往使民背負。

translations.literal: On the nine frontiers grain was mostly delivered by cart; in Xuande, supplying Kaiping was the same, but Lanzhou, Gansu, and Songpan often made civilians carry on their backs.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier grain mostly moved by cart—Kaiping in Xuande followed the same pattern—but Lanzhou, Gansu, and Songpan often used human porters.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，又嘗令廣東海運二十萬石給交址云。

translations.literal: In Yongle they also once ordered Guangdong to sea-transport 200,000 shi to Jiaozhi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle Guangdong once sea-transported 200,000 shi to Jiaozhi as well.

sentences.zh: 明初，京衛有軍儲倉。

translations.literal: Early Ming capital guards had army store depots.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming capital garrisons maintained army grain depots.

sentences.zh: 洪武三年增置至二十所，且建臨濠、臨清二倉以供轉運。

translations.literal: In Hongwu 3 they were increased to twenty sites, and Linhuo and Linqing depots were built to support relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 3 expanded them to twenty sites and built Linhuo and Linqing depots for relay hauls.

sentences.zh: 各行省有倉，官吏俸取給焉。

translations.literal: Each province had depots from which official salaries were drawn.
translations.idiomatic: Every province kept depots that supplied officials' salaries.

sentences.zh: 邊境有倉，收屯田所入以給軍。

translations.literal: Frontier regions had depots collecting garrison-farm yields to supply troops.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier garrisons kept depots fed by military colony harvests.

sentences.zh: 州縣則設預備倉，東南西北四所，以振凶荒。

translations.literal: Counties and prefectures set up reserve depots—four in southeast, northwest, etc.—to relieve famine.
translations.idiomatic: Counties and prefectures maintained reserve depots in all directions to relieve famine.

sentences.zh: 自鈔法行，頗有省革。

translations.literal: After paper money was implemented, many were reduced or abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Paper currency reduced the need for many of these depots.

sentences.zh: 二十四年儲糧十六萬石於臨清，以給訓練騎兵。

translations.literal: In year 24, 160,000 shi were stored at Linqing to supply drill cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Year 24 stored 160,000 shi at Linqing for drill cavalry.

sentences.zh: 二十八年置皇城四門倉，儲糧給守禦軍。

translations.literal: In year 28 the four gates of the imperial city gained depots storing grain for defensive garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Year 28 added depots at the imperial city's four gates for the defensive garrisons.

sentences.zh: 增京師諸衛倉凡四十一。

translations.literal: Capital guard depots were increased to forty-one in all.
translations.idiomatic: Capital garrison depots were expanded to forty-one.

sentences.zh: 又設北平、密雲諸縣倉，儲糧以資北征。

translations.literal: Depots were also established in Beiping, Miyun, and other counties, storing grain to support northern campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Depots at Beiping, Miyun, and other counties stockpiled grain for northern campaigns.

sentences.zh: 永樂中，置天津及通州左衛倉，且設北京三十七衛倉。

translations.literal: During the Yongle reign, the Tianjin depot and the Tongzhou Left Guard depot were established, and thirty-seven guard depots were set up in Beijing.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle the court opened depots at Tianjin and the Tongzhou Left Guard post and established thirty-seven garrison grain stores across Beijing.

sentences.zh: 益令天下府縣多設倉儲，預備倉之在四鄉者移置城內。

translations.literal: It further ordered prefectures and counties throughout the realm to establish many storehouses, and reserve depots in the four townships were moved inside the cities.
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered prefectures and counties empire-wide to expand storage, moving reserve granaries that had stood in outlying villages into county seats.

sentences.zh: 迨會通河成，始設倉於徐州、淮安、德州，而臨清因洪武之舊，並天津倉凡五，謂之水次倉，以資轉運。

translations.literal: When the Hui Tong Canal was completed, depots were first set up at Xuzhou, Huai'an, and Dezhou; Linqing continued the Hongwu arrangement; together with the Tianjin depot there were five in all, called landing depots, to supply relay transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Hui Tong Canal opened, depots went up at Xuzhou, Huai'an, and Dezhou; Linqing kept its Hongwu-era site; with Tianjin that made five landing depots to feed grain transport.

sentences.zh: 既，又移德州倉於臨清之永清壩，設武清衛倉於河西務，設通州衛倉於張家灣。

translations.literal: Afterward the Dezhou depot was moved to Yongqing Dam at Linqing; a Wuqing Guard depot was set up at Hexiwu; a Tongzhou Guard depot at Zhangjiawan.
translations.idiomatic: The Dezhou depot was later relocated to Yongqing Dam near Linqing; Wuqing Guard got a depot at Hexiwu and Tongzhou Guard one at Zhangjiawan.

sentences.zh: 宣德中，增造臨清倉，容三百萬石。

translations.literal: During the Xuande reign, the Linqing depot was expanded, with capacity for three million shi.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande expanded the Linqing depot to hold three million shi.

sentences.zh: 增置北京及通州倉。

translations.literal: Beijing and Tongzhou depots were additionally established.
translations.idiomatic: More depots were added in Beijing and Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 京倉以御史、戶部官、錦衣千百戶季更巡察。

translations.literal: Capital depots were inspected in rotation each season by censors, Ministry of Revenue officials, and Jinyi guard officers of qian and bai rank.
translations.idiomatic: Capital granaries were inspected in quarterly rotation by censors, Revenue officials, and Jinyi guard officers of thousand- and hundred-man rank.

sentences.zh: 外倉則佈政、按察、都司關防之。

translations.literal: Outer depots were sealed and guarded by provincial administration commissioners, surveillance commissioners, and regional military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Outlying depots came under the joint seals of provincial governors, surveillance commissioners, and regional military commanders.

sentences.zh: 各倉門，以致仕武官二，率老幼軍丁十人守之，半年一更。

translations.literal: At each depot gate, two retired military officers led ten old and young soldier conscripts to guard it, rotating every half year.
translations.idiomatic: Each depot gate was held by two retired officers commanding ten veteran and junior soldiers, rotated every six months.

sentences.zh: 英宗初，命廷臣集議，天下司府州縣，有倉者以衛所倉屬之，無倉者以衛所改隸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Yingzong's reign, court ministers were ordered to confer: throughout the realm's prefectures, subprefectures, and counties, where there were depots the guard-post depots were placed under them; where there were none, guard posts were reassigned in subordination.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yingzong's reign the throne ordered a court conference: wherever a prefecture or county already had granaries, nearby guard-post stores were placed under it; where none existed, guard posts were reassigned accordingly.

sentences.zh: 惟遼東、甘肅、寧夏、萬全及沿海衛所，無府州縣者仍其舊。

translations.literal: Only in Liaodong, Gansu, Ningxia, Wanquan, and coastal guard posts without prefectures or counties did things remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Liaodong, Gansu, Ningxia, Wanquan, and coastal guard posts without county administration kept the old arrangement.

sentences.zh: 正統中，增置京衛倉凡七。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign, seven capital-guard depots were additionally set up.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong added seven capital garrison depots.

sentences.zh: 自兌運法行，諸倉支運者少，而京、通倉不能容，乃毀臨清、德州、河西務倉三分之一，改為京、通倉。

translations.literal: Since exchange transport was implemented, relay transport through the various depots grew rare, yet Beijing and Tong depots could not hold the grain; so one-third of the Linqing, Dezhou, and Hexiwu depots was destroyed and converted into Beijing and Tong depots.
translations.idiomatic: Once exchange transport prevailed, relay hauls through transit depots dwindled while Beijing and Tongzhou still lacked space; a third of the Linqing, Dezhou, and Hexiwu stores was torn down and rebuilt as capital depots.

sentences.zh: 景泰初，移武清衛諸倉於通州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jingtai reign, the Wuqing Guard depots were moved to Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai moved the Wuqing Guard depots to Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 成化初，廢臨、德預備倉在城外者，而以城內空廒儲預備米。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Chenghua reign, the Linqing and Dezhou reserve depots outside the walls were abolished, and empty granaries inside the cities were used to store reserve rice.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua closed the Linqing and Dezhou reserve granaries outside the walls and filled vacant city silos with emergency rice.

sentences.zh: 名臨清者曰常盈，德州者曰常豐。

translations.literal: That at Linqing was named Changying; that at Dezhou, Changfeng.
translations.idiomatic: The Linqing store was renamed Changying ("Ever Full") and the Dezhou store Changfeng ("Ever Plentiful").

sentences.zh: 凡京倉五十有六，通倉十有六。

translations.literal: In all there were fifty-six capital depots and sixteen Tong depots.
translations.idiomatic: Beijing had fifty-six granaries and Tongzhou sixteen.

sentences.zh: 直省府州縣、籓府、邊隘、堡站、衛所屯戍皆有倉，少者一二，多者二三十云。

translations.literal: Directly administered provinces' prefectures, subprefectures, and counties, princely establishments, frontier passes, fortress stations, and guard-post garrisons all had depots—one or two at the fewest, twenty or thirty at most, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Every province, princely estate, frontier pass, station, and garrison maintained its own stores—anywhere from one or two to as many as twenty or thirty.

sentences.zh: 預備倉之設也，太祖選耆民運鈔糴米，以備振濟，即令掌之。

translations.literal: As for establishing reserve depots: the Founder selected elderly commoners to transport paper money and purchase rice for relief stores, and immediately put them in charge.
translations.idiomatic: When reserve granaries were first created, Hongwu picked respected elders to deliver cash and buy grain for famine relief, putting them in charge on the spot.

sentences.zh: 天下州縣多所儲蓄，後漸廢馳。

translations.literal: Prefectures and counties throughout the realm stored much, but later this gradually fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: Counties once kept substantial reserves, but the practice gradually lapsed.

sentences.zh: 于謙撫河南、山西，修其政。

translations.literal: Yu Qian, as grand coordinator of Henan and Shanxi, restored the policy.
translations.idiomatic: As grand coordinator of Henan and Shanxi, Yu Qian revived it.

sentences.zh: 周忱撫南畿，別立濟農倉。

translations.literal: Zhou Chen, as grand coordinator of the Southern Capital region, separately established relief-farming depots.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chen, coordinating the Southern Capital region, set up separate relief-farming granaries.

sentences.zh: 他人不能也。

translations.literal: Others could not do likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Few others matched their success.

sentences.zh: 正統時，重侵盜之罪，至僉妻充軍。

translations.literal: During the Zhengtong reign the crime of embezzlement and theft was heavily punished, extending even to impressing the offender's wife for frontier service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong made embezzlement a capital offense—even the thief's wife could be impressed for military service.

sentences.zh: 且定納穀千五百石者，敕獎為義民，免本戶雜役。

translations.literal: Moreover it was fixed that those donating 1,500 shi of grain would be commended by imperial rescript as public-spirited commoners, exempt from miscellaneous corvee for their household.
translations.idiomatic: Donors of 1,500 shi earned an imperial commendation as "righteous commoners" and exemption from miscellaneous corvee.

sentences.zh: 凡振饑米一石，俟有年，納稻穀二石五斗還官。

translations.literal: For every shi of famine-relief rice, when years were good one paid back two shi five dou of paddy to the government.
translations.idiomatic: Every shi lent for famine relief was repaid after a good harvest at two shi five dou of unmilled grain.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年限州縣十里以下積萬五千石，二十里積二萬石；

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 3 set limits for prefectures and counties: within ten li, accumulation of 15,000 shi; within twenty li, 20,000 shi;
