translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 3 fixed reserve targets: counties within ten li had to stock 15,000 shi; within twenty li, 20,000 shi;

sentences.zh: 衛千戶所萬五千石，百戶所三百石。

translations.literal: Guard thousand-household posts 15,000 shi, hundred-household posts 300 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-man guard posts 15,000 shi, hundred-man posts 300 shi.

sentences.zh: 考滿之日，稽其多寡以為殿最。

translations.literal: At the end of a term's evaluation, the amount stocked was checked to determine ranking last or first.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end officials were ranked according to how much they had stocked.

sentences.zh: 不及三分者奪俸，六分以上降調。

translations.literal: Those falling short by three-tenths had salary withheld; those six-tenths short were demoted and transferred.
translations.idiomatic: Falling three-tenths short cost an official his salary; six-tenths or more brought demotion.

sentences.zh: 十八年令贖罪贓罰，皆糴穀入倉。

translations.literal: In year eighteen it was ordered that redemption fines and forfeiture penalties all be converted to purchased grain entering the depot.
translations.idiomatic: Year eighteen required all fines and forfeits to be paid as grain into reserve stores.

sentences.zh: 正德中，令囚納紙者，以其八折米入倉。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign, those ordered to pay paper as a penalty had four-fifths of it converted to rice entering the depot.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde allowed paper penalties to be commuted: eighty percent paid as grain.

sentences.zh: 軍官有犯者，納谷準立功。

translations.literal: Military officers who violated the law could atone by paying grain equivalent to meritorious service.
translations.idiomatic: Delinquent officers could buy off punishment with grain donations counted as merit.

sentences.zh: 初，預備倉皆設倉官，至是革，令州縣官及管糧倉官領其事。

translations.literal: At first reserve depots all had depot officers; now these were abolished and the matter was entrusted to prefecture and county officials and grain-depot officers.
translations.idiomatic: Reserve granaries had once had dedicated clerks, but that post was abolished and county magistrates plus grain officers took over.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，諭德顧鼎臣言：「成、弘時，每年以存留餘米入預備倉，緩急有備。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiajing reign, Tutor Gu Dingchen said: "In the Chenghua and Hongzhi reigns, each year retained surplus rice went into reserve depots, so that in emergency there was provision.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Jiajing, Tutor Gu Dingchen said: "Under Chenghua and Hongzhi, surplus rice was set aside each year for reserve granaries, so emergencies could be met.

sentences.zh: 今秋糧僅足兌運，預備無粒米。

translations.literal: Now autumn grain barely suffices for exchange transport; the reserves have not a grain of rice.
translations.idiomatic: Now autumn tribute barely covers exchange transport, and the reserves hold not a grain of rice.

sentences.zh: 一遇災傷，輒奏留他糧及勸富民借谷，以應故事。

translations.literal: Whenever disaster or crop failure occurred, memorials immediately asked to retain other grain and urge wealthy households to lend grain, merely to answer the formal requirement.
translations.idiomatic: At the first sign of disaster, officials merely memorialized to hold back other grain and urge the wealthy to lend—going through the motions of old precedent.

sentences.zh: 乞急復預備倉糧以裕民。」

translations.literal: I beg urgently to restore reserve-grain stocks to enlarge the people's welfare.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that reserve stocks be restored at once to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 帝乃令有司設法多積米穀，仍仿古常平法，春振貧民，秋成還官，不取其息。

translations.literal: The emperor then ordered the officials to devise methods to accumulate much rice and grain, still following the ancient ever-normal method: in spring relieve the poor, at autumn harvest return to the government, taking no interest.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then ordered local officials to stockpile grain by the ancient ever-normal method: lend to the poor in spring, collect repayment after harvest, and charge no interest.

sentences.zh: 府積萬石，州四五千石，縣二三千石為率。

translations.literal: Prefectures accumulated 10,000 shi as standard; subprefectures four or five thousand; counties two or three thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Targets were 10,000 shi for prefectures, four or five thousand for subprefectures, and two or three thousand for counties.

sentences.zh: 既，又定十里以下萬五千石，累而上之，八百里以下至十九萬石。

translations.literal: Afterward it was further fixed that within ten li 15,000 shi, accumulating upward; within eight hundred li up to 190,000 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Later quotas scaled by distance: 15,000 shi within ten li, rising in steps to 190,000 shi within eight hundred li.

sentences.zh: 其後積粟盡平糶，以濟貧民，儲積漸減。

translations.literal: Afterward stored grain was all sold at fair price to aid the poor, and reserves gradually diminished.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the stockpiles were sold off at fair price to aid the poor, and reserves steadily shrank.

sentences.zh: 隆慶時，劇郡無過六千石，小邑止千石。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign large prefectures had no more than 6,000 shi, small counties only 1,000.
translations.idiomatic: By Longqing even major prefectures held no more than 6,000 shi and small counties only 1,000.

sentences.zh: 久之數益減，科罰亦益輕。

translations.literal: Over time the numbers diminished still further, and administrative penalties grew lighter.
translations.idiomatic: Over time stocks fell further and penalties for failure grew lighter.

sentences.zh: 萬曆中，上州郡至三千石止，而小邑或僅百石。

translations.literal: During the Wanli reign major prefectures stopped at 3,000 shi, while small counties sometimes had only 100 shi.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wanli major prefectures topped out at 3,000 shi and some small counties held barely 100.

sentences.zh: 有司沿為具文，屢下詔申飭，率以虛數欺罔而已。

translations.literal: Local officials treated these as empty formalities; repeated edicts enjoined them, but they mostly deceived with fictitious numbers.
translations.idiomatic: Officials treated the quotas as empty paperwork; repeated edicts changed nothing—they reported fictitious totals.

sentences.zh: 弘治中，江西巡撫林俊嘗請建常平及社倉。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign, Jiangxi grand coordinator Lin Jun once asked to establish ever-normal and community granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, Jiangxi grand coordinator Lin Jun proposed ever-normal and community granaries.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖八年乃令各撫、按設社倉。

translations.literal: In Jiajing 8 each grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner was ordered to set up community granaries.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 8 ordered every grand coordinator and surveillance commissioner to establish community granaries.

sentences.zh: 令民二三十家為一社，擇家殷實而有行義者一人為社首，處事公平者一人為社正，能書算者一人為社副，每朔望會集，別戶上中下，出米四斗至一斗有差，鬥加耗五合，上戶主其事。

translations.literal: Twenty or thirty households were grouped as one community; one person from a wealthy and righteous family was chosen as community head; one who handled affairs fairly as community director; one skilled in writing and calculation as deputy; they met each new and full moon, distinguished households as upper, middle, and lower, each contributing from four dou down to one dou according to rank, with five ge wastage added per dou; upper households presided over the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Households were grouped in communities of twenty or thirty; each chose a wealthy and upright head, a fair-minded director, and a literate deputy who could keep accounts. They met at every new and full moon, ranked members upper, middle, or lower, and collected from four dou down to one dou per household according to rank, adding five ge of wastage per dou; upper households ran the operation.

sentences.zh: 年饑，上戶不足者量貸，稔歲還倉。

translations.literal: In famine years upper households lent as needed to those who fell short; in good years they returned grain to the depot.
translations.idiomatic: In famine years the well-off lent to those in need; after a good harvest the grain was returned to the community store.

sentences.zh: 中下戶酌量振給，不還倉。

translations.literal: For middle and lower households relief was given as appropriate, not returned to the depot.
translations.idiomatic: Middle and lower households received relief as needed, with no repayment required.

sentences.zh: 有司造冊送撫、按，歲一察覈。

translations.literal: Local officials prepared registers sent to grand coordinators and surveillance commissioners, with annual inspection.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials kept registers for the coordinators and surveillance commissioners, who audited them once a year.

sentences.zh: 倉虛，罰社首出一歲之米。

translations.literal: If the depot was empty, the community head was fined one year's rice.
translations.idiomatic: If a store ran empty, the community head paid a fine of one year's rice.

sentences.zh: 其法頗善，然其後無力行者。

translations.literal: The method was quite good, but afterward none had the strength to implement it.
translations.idiomatic: The scheme was sound, but in time no one had the means to carry it out.

sentences.zh: 兩京庫藏，先後建設，其制大略相同。

translations.literal: Treasuries of the Two Capitals were built successively; their systems were broadly the same.
translations.idiomatic: The Two Capitals built their treasuries in stages, on broadly similar lines.

sentences.zh: 內府凡十庫：內承運庫，貯緞匹、金銀、寶玉、齒角、羽毛，而金花銀最大，歲進百萬兩有奇。

translations.literal: The inner palace had ten treasuries in all: the Inner Reception Treasury stored silk lengths, gold, silver, jade, ivory, horns, and feathers; flower-pattern silver was the largest item, with yearly entry of more than one million taels.
translations.idiomatic: The inner palace maintained ten treasuries. The Inner Reception Treasury held silk, gold, silver, jade, ivory, horns, and feathers; flower-pattern silver was the largest item, with annual intake exceeding one million taels.

sentences.zh: 廣積庫，貯硫黃、硝石。

translations.literal: The Broad Accumulation Treasury stored sulfur and saltpeter.
translations.idiomatic: The Broad Accumulation Treasury held sulfur and saltpeter.

sentences.zh: 甲字形檔，貯布匹、顏料。

translations.literal: The Jia-shaped archive stored cloth lengths and pigments.
translations.idiomatic: The Jia-shaped archive stored cloth and pigments.

sentences.zh: 乙字形檔，貯胖襖、戰鞋、軍士裘帽。

translations.literal: The Yi-shaped archive stored padded jackets, battle shoes, and soldiers' fur hats.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi-shaped archive held padded jackets, battle shoes, and soldiers' fur caps.

sentences.zh: 丙字形檔，貯棉花、絲纊。

translations.literal: The Bing-shaped archive stored cotton and silk floss.
translations.idiomatic: The Bing-shaped archive held cotton and silk floss.

sentences.zh: 丁字形檔，貯銅鐵、獸皮、蘇木。

translations.literal: The Ding-shaped archive stored copper, iron, hides, and sappanwood.
translations.idiomatic: The Ding-shaped archive held copper, iron, hides, and sappanwood.

sentences.zh: 戊字形檔，貯甲仗。

translations.literal: The Wu-shaped archive stored armor and weapons.
translations.idiomatic: The Wu-shaped archive held armor and weapons.

sentences.zh: 贓罰庫，貯沒官物。

translations.literal: The Forfeiture Treasury stored confiscated government property.
translations.idiomatic: The Forfeiture Treasury held confiscated goods.

sentences.zh: 廣惠庫，貯錢鈔。

translations.literal: The Broad Benefit Treasury stored paper money.
translations.idiomatic: The Broad Benefit Treasury held paper money.

sentences.zh: 廣盈庫，貯紵絲、紗羅、綾錦、槹絹。

translations.literal: The Broad Surplus Treasury stored ramie silk, gauze, brocade, and silk fabrics.
translations.idiomatic: The Broad Surplus Treasury held ramie silk, gauze, brocade, and silk fabrics.

sentences.zh: 六庫皆屬戶部，惟乙字形檔屬兵部，戊字、廣積、廣盈庫屬工部。

translations.literal: Six treasuries all belonged to the Ministry of Revenue; only the Yi-shaped archive belonged to the Ministry of War; the Wu-shaped, Broad Accumulation, and Broad Surplus treasuries belonged to the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Six treasuries fell under Revenue; the Yi-shaped archive under War; and the Wu-shaped, Broad Accumulation, and Broad Surplus treasuries under Works.

sentences.zh: 又有天財庫，亦名司鑰庫，貯各衙門管鑰，亦貯錢鈔。

translations.literal: There was also the Heavenly Wealth Treasury, also called the Key Treasury, storing keys from the various offices, and also storing paper money.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the Heavenly Wealth Treasury, or Key Treasury, which held keys from every office as well as paper money.

sentences.zh: 供用庫，貯粳稻、熟米及上供物。

translations.literal: The Supply Treasury stored glutinous rice, prepared rice, and tribute supplies.
translations.idiomatic: The Supply Treasury held glutinous rice, prepared rice, and items for imperial tribute.

sentences.zh: 以上通謂之內庫。

translations.literal: The above were collectively called the inner treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: All of these were known collectively as the inner treasuries.

sentences.zh: 其在宮內者，又有內東裕庫、寶藏庫，謂之裏庫。

translations.literal: Those inside the palace included the Inner Eastern Abundance Treasury and the Treasure Treasury, called the inner-inner treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Inside the palace itself were the Inner Eastern Abundance Treasury and the Treasure Treasury—the so-called inner-inner treasuries.

sentences.zh: 凡裏庫不關於有司。

translations.literal: The inner-inner treasuries had no connection to regular officials.
translations.idiomatic: The inner-inner treasuries lay outside regular official oversight.

sentences.zh: 其會歸門、寶善門迤東及南城磁器諸庫，則謂之外庫。

translations.literal: Those from Huigui Gate, east of Baoshan Gate, and the porcelain treasuries of the southern city were called the outer treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Treasuries east of Huigui and Baoshan Gates and the southern city's porcelain stores were called the outer treasuries.

sentences.zh: 若內府諸監司局，神樂堂，犧牲所，太常、光祿寺，國子監，皆各以所掌，收貯應用諸物。

translations.literal: The inner palace directorates, bureaus, and offices, the Music Hall, the Sacrifice Office, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the Imperial Academy each stored supplies according to their jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Inner palace directorates and bureaus, the Music Hall, Sacrifice Office, Court of Imperial Sacrifices, Court of Imperial Entertainments, and Imperial Academy each kept stores for their own needs.

sentences.zh: 太僕則馬價銀歸之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Stud collected horse-price silver.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Stud received horse-price silver.

sentences.zh: 明初，嘗置行用庫於京城及諸府州縣，以收易昏爛之鈔。

translations.literal: Early in the Ming, circulation treasuries were set up in the capital and in prefectures, subprefectures, and counties to collect worn and tattered paper money for exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Early Ming established circulation treasuries in the capital and across the provinces to swap out worn paper notes.

sentences.zh: 仁宗時罷。

translations.literal: They were abolished during the Renzong reign.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong abolished them.

sentences.zh: 英宗時，始設太倉庫。

translations.literal: During the Yingzong reign, the Taicang Treasury was first established.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yingzong the Taicang Treasury was first established.

sentences.zh: 初，歲賦不徵金銀，惟坑冶稅有金銀，入內承運庫。

translations.literal: At first annual levies did not collect gold and silver; only mining and smelting taxes had gold and silver, entering the Inner Reception Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: At first annual levies brought in no gold or silver; only mining taxes did, and those went to the Inner Reception Treasury.

sentences.zh: 其歲賦偶折金銀者，俱送南京供武臣祿。

translations.literal: When annual levies were occasionally commuted to gold and silver, all were sent to Nanjing to supply military stipends.
translations.idiomatic: When tribute was occasionally commuted to gold or silver, it all went to Nanjing for military stipends.

sentences.zh: 而各邊有緩急，亦取足其中。

translations.literal: When the frontiers had emergencies, they were also supplied from there.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier emergencies were also met from those funds.

sentences.zh: 正統元年改折漕糧，歲以百萬為額，盡解內承運庫，不復送南京。

translations.literal: In Zhengtong 1 grain tribute was changed to silver commutation, with one million taels as the yearly quota, all submitted to the Inner Reception Treasury, no longer sent to Nanjing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 1 commuted canal tribute to silver at one million taels a year, all routed to the Inner Reception Treasury instead of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 自給武臣祿十餘萬兩外，皆為御用。

translations.literal: Beyond the hundred thousand-odd taels for military stipends, all was for imperial use.
translations.idiomatic: Aside from roughly 100,000 taels for military pay, the rest went to the imperial household.

sentences.zh: 所謂金花銀也。

translations.literal: This was what was called flower-pattern silver.
translations.idiomatic: This was flower-pattern silver.

sentences.zh: 七年乃設戶部太倉庫。

translations.literal: In year seven the Ministry of Revenue Taicang Treasury was established.
translations.idiomatic: Year seven saw the creation of the Ministry of Revenue's Taicang Treasury.

sentences.zh: 各直省派剩麥米，十庫中綿絲、絹布及馬草、鹽課、關稅，凡折銀者，皆入太倉庫。

translations.literal: Surplus wheat and rice from the provinces, silk and cloth from the ten treasuries, horse fodder, salt levies, and customs duties—all silver commutation went into the Taicang Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial surplus grain, silk and cloth from the ten treasuries, horse fodder, salt levies, customs duties—every silver commutation flowed into Taicang.

sentences.zh: 籍沒家財，變賣田產，追收店錢，援例上納者，亦皆入焉。

translations.literal: Confiscated family wealth, sold fields and estates, recovered shop payments, and precedent contributions also all entered it.
translations.idiomatic: Confiscated estates, sold property, recovered shop debts, and precedent contributions all went there as well.

sentences.zh: 專以貯銀，故又謂之銀庫。

translations.literal: It was dedicated to storing silver, and so was also called the silver treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated to silver alone, it was also called the silver treasury.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，內府供應繁多，每收太倉銀入內庫。

translations.literal: During the Hongzhi reign inner palace demands multiplied, and Taicang silver was repeatedly drawn into the inner treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi the inner palace's demands multiplied, and Taicang silver was repeatedly siphoned into the inner treasuries.

sentences.zh: 又置南京銀庫。

translations.literal: A Nanjing silver treasury was also established.
translations.idiomatic: A Nanjing silver treasury was added as well.

sentences.zh: 正德時，內承運庫中官數言內府財用不充，請支太倉銀。

translations.literal: During the Zhengde reign eunuchs of the Inner Reception Treasury repeatedly said inner palace funds were insufficient and asked to draw Taicang silver.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, Inner Reception eunuchs repeatedly complained that palace funds were insufficient and petitioned to draw on Taicang silver.

sentences.zh: 戶部執奏不能沮。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue memorialized in opposition but could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Revenue protested in memorials but could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖初，內府供應視弘治時，其後乃倍之。

translations.literal: Early in the Jiajing reign inner palace supplies matched the Hongzhi level; afterward they doubled.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jiajing palace spending matched Hongzhi levels; later it doubled.

sentences.zh: 初，太倉中庫積銀八百餘萬兩，續收者貯之兩廡，以便支發。

translations.literal: At first the central vault of Taicang accumulated more than eight million taels of silver; continuing receipts were stored in the two side wings for convenient disbursement.
translations.idiomatic: At first Taicang's central vault held more than eight million taels; new receipts went to side wings for easier disbursement.

sentences.zh: 而中庫不動，遂以中庫為老庫，兩廡為外庫。

translations.literal: The central vault was left untouched, and so the central vault was called the old vault and the two side wings the outer vault.
translations.idiomatic: The central vault stayed untouched and became the old vault; the side wings served as the outer vault.

sentences.zh: 及是時，老庫所存者僅百二十萬兩。

translations.literal: By this time the old vault held only 1.2 million taels.
translations.idiomatic: By then the old vault held only 1.2 million taels.

sentences.zh: 二十二年特令金花、子粒銀應解內庫者，並送太倉備邊用，然其後復入內庫。

translations.literal: In year twenty-two a special order directed flower-pattern silver and grain-tax silver that should have gone to the inner treasuries all to be sent to Taicang for frontier use; afterward it reverted to the inner treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Year twenty-two ordered flower-pattern and grain-tax silver destined for the inner treasuries sent to Taicang for frontier use instead—but the flow soon reversed.

sentences.zh: 三十七年令歲進內庫銀百萬兩外，加預備欽取銀，後又取沒官銀四十萬兩入內庫。

translations.literal: In year thirty-seven, beyond the one million taels yearly sent to the inner treasuries, reserve silver for imperial withdrawal was added; later four hundred thousand taels of confiscated silver were also taken into the inner treasuries.
translations.idiomatic: Year thirty-seven added reserve silver for imperial withdrawal on top of the million taels sent yearly to the inner treasuries; later four hundred thousand taels of confiscated silver followed.

sentences.zh: 隆慶中，數取太倉銀入內庫，承運庫中官至以空紮下戶部取之。

translations.literal: During the Longqing reign Taicang silver was repeatedly drawn into the inner treasuries; Reception Treasury eunuchs even sent empty vouchers down to the Ministry of Revenue to collect it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Longqing Taicang silver was repeatedly drained into the inner treasuries; Reception eunuchs even sent blank vouchers to Revenue to collect it.

sentences.zh: 廷臣疏諫，皆不聽。

translations.literal: Court ministers memorialized in remonstrance; none of it was heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Court ministers remonstrated in memorials; the throne paid no heed.

sentences.zh: 又數取光祿太僕銀，工部尚書硃衡極諫，不聽。

translations.literal: Silver from the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the Imperial Stud was also repeatedly taken; Works Minister Zhu Heng remonstrated fiercely; it was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: Silver from the Court of Imperial Entertainments and the Imperial Stud was seized repeatedly as well; Works Minister Zhu Heng protested fiercely, to no avail.

sentences.zh: 初，世宗時，太倉所入二百萬兩有奇。

translations.literal: At first, in the Jiajing reign, Taicang receipts were a little over two million taels.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiajing reign, Taicang Treasury receipts totaled a little over two million taels.

sentences.zh: 至神宗萬曆六年，太倉歲入凡四百五十餘萬兩，而內庫歲供金花銀外，又增買辦銀二十萬兩以為常，後又加內操馬芻料銀七萬餘兩。

translations.literal: By the sixth year of Wanli under the Shenzong Emperor, Taicang's annual intake was more than 4.5 million taels; besides the inner treasury's annual flower-pattern silver, another two hundred thousand taels for purchases was made regular, and later more than seventy thousand taels for inner-guard horse fodder was added.
translations.idiomatic: By Wanli 6 under Emperor Shenzong, Taicang's annual intake exceeded 4.5 million taels; beyond the inner treasury's regular flower-pattern silver, another two hundred thousand taels for palace purchases became fixed, and later more than seventy thousand taels for inner-guard horse fodder was added.

sentences.zh: 久之，太倉、光祿、太僕銀，括取幾盡。

translations.literal: After a long time silver from Taicang, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the Court of the Imperial Stud was swept up almost entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Over time silver from Taicang, the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and the Court of the Imperial Stud was drained almost completely.

sentences.zh: 邊賞首功，向發內庫者，亦取之太僕矣。

translations.literal: Frontier rewards for first merit, which had formerly been paid from the inner treasury, were also taken from the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier rewards for first merit in battle, once paid from the inner treasury, were now drawn from the Imperial Stud as well.

sentences.zh: 凡甲字諸庫，主事偕科道巡視。

translations.literal: All the Jia-form storehouses were inspected by section chiefs together with censorate and surveillance officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Jia-form storehouses were inspected jointly by section chiefs and censorate officials.

sentences.zh: 太倉庫，員外郎、主事領之，而以給事中巡視。

translations.literal: The Taicang Treasury was led by vice directors and section chiefs, with supervising secretaries conducting inspections.
translations.idiomatic: The Taicang Treasury was managed by vice directors and section chiefs under the oversight of supervising secretaries.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖中，始兩月一報出納之數。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign reporting of receipts and disbursements every two months was first instituted.
translations.idiomatic: During Jiajing, receipts and disbursements were first reported every two months.

sentences.zh: 時修工部舊庫，名曰節慎庫，以貯礦銀。

translations.literal: At that time the old Ministry of Works storehouse was repaired and named the Frugal-Care Treasury to store mining silver.
translations.idiomatic: The old Ministry of Works storehouse was then repaired and renamed the Frugal-Care Treasury to hold mining silver.

sentences.zh: 尚書文明以給工價，帝詰責之，令以他銀補償，自是專以給內用焉。

translations.literal: Minister Wen Ming used it to pay construction costs; the emperor rebuked him and ordered other silver to make compensation, and from then on it was devoted solely to inner-court use.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Wen Ming spent it on construction wages; the emperor rebuked him and ordered repayment from other funds, after which the treasury was reserved solely for palace use.

sentences.zh: 其在外諸布政司、都司、直省府州縣衛所皆有庫，以貯金銀、錢鈔、絲帛、贓罰諸物。

translations.literal: Outside, every provincial administration commission, regional military commission, and prefecture, county, and guard post under direct provinces had storehouses to hold gold, silver, paper money, silk, confiscated goods, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: Across the provinces, every administration commission, regional command, prefecture, county, and guard maintained storehouses for gold, silver, paper notes, silk, fines, and confiscated goods.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史三歲一盤查。

translations.literal: Touring censors conducted inventories every three years.
translations.idiomatic: Touring censors audited them every three years.

sentences.zh: 各運司皆有庫貯銀，歲終，巡鹽御史委官察之。

translations.literal: Every salt transport commission had a treasury storing silver; at year's end the salt-circuit censor delegated officials to inspect it.
translations.idiomatic: Every salt transport commission kept a silver treasury inspected at year-end by officials delegated by the salt-circuit censor.

sentences.zh: 凡府州縣稅課司局、河泊所，歲課、商稅、魚課、引由、契本諸課程，太祖令所司解州縣府司，以至於部，部劄之庫，其元封識，不擅發也。

translations.literal: For all tax offices, commercial-tax bureaus, and fishing stations in prefectures and counties—annual levies, commercial taxes, fish taxes, licenses, deed fees, and other charges—the founding emperor ordered the responsible offices to remit through county, prefecture, and provincial offices up to the ministry, which sealed them in the treasury with original seals and did not disburse without authorization.
translations.idiomatic: For tax offices, commercial-tax bureaus, and fishing stations in every prefecture and county—annual levies, commercial taxes, fish taxes, licenses, and deed fees—the Hongwu Emperor required remittance up through county and provincial offices to the ministry, which sealed receipts in the treasury and released nothing without authorization.

sentences.zh: 至永樂時，始委驗勘，中，方起解；

translations.literal: By the Yongle reign inspection and verification were first delegated; only after passing were remittances initiated;
translations.idiomatic: Under Yongle, inspection was required first; only after approval could remittances begin;

sentences.zh: 至部復驗，同，乃進納。

translations.literal: at the ministry they were verified again, and if matching, then submitted.
translations.idiomatic: and at the ministry they were verified again before final acceptance.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖時，建驗試廳，驗中，給進狀寄庫。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign an inspection hall was built; after passing inspection, a submission certificate was issued and goods held in the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiajing an inspection hall was built; approved goods received submission certificates and were held in the treasury.

sentences.zh: 月逢九，會巡視庫藏科道官，進庫驗收，不堪者駁易。

translations.literal: On days ending in nine each month, censorate officials overseeing treasuries assembled, entered the storehouses to inspect and accept, and rejected and replaced what was unfit.
translations.idiomatic: On every ninth day of the month, censorate treasury inspectors assembled, entered the storehouses to accept goods, and rejected substandard items for replacement.

sentences.zh: 正統十年設通濟庫於通州。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhengtong the Tongji Treasury was established at Tongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhengtong 10 the Tongji Treasury was established at Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 世宗時罷。

translations.literal: It was abolished in the Jiajing reign.
translations.idiomatic: It was abolished under Emperor Jiajing.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，密雲、薊州、昌平諸鎮皆設庫，收貯主客年例、軍門公費及撫賞、修邊銀云。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing, Miyun, Jizhou, Changping, and other garrisons all established treasuries to receive and store annual quotas for hosts and guests, military-gate public funds, pacification rewards, and frontier-repair silver.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing, Miyun, Jizhou, Changping, and other garrisons established treasuries for annual host-and-guest quotas, military-gate funds, pacification rewards, and frontier-repair silver.

sentences.zh: 凡為倉庫害者，莫如中官。

translations.literal: Of all who harmed storehouses and treasuries, none matched palace eunuchs.
translations.idiomatic: No one harmed granaries and treasuries more than palace eunuchs.

sentences.zh: 內府諸庫監收者，橫索無厭。

translations.literal: Those who supervised collection at the inner-palace treasuries extorted without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Supervisors at inner-palace treasuries extorted without limit.

sentences.zh: 正德時，台州衛指揮陳良納軍器，稽留八載，至乞食於市。

translations.literal: In the Zhengde reign Taizhou Guard Commander Chen Liang delivered military equipment; it was held up eight years until he was begging in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhengde, Taizhou Guard Commander Chen Liang delivered military equipment that was held eight years—until he was reduced to begging in the streets.

sentences.zh: 內府收糧，增耗嘗以數倍為率，其患如此。

translations.literal: When the inner palace received grain, surplus allowances were often several times the statutory rate—such was the harm.
translations.idiomatic: When the inner palace received grain, surplus allowances often ran several times the statutory rate—such was the abuse.

sentences.zh: 諸倉初不設中官，宣德末，京、通二倉始置總督中官一人，後淮、徐、臨、德諸倉亦置監督，漕輓軍民被其害。

translations.literal: At first the various warehouses had no eunuch officials; late in Xuande one supervising eunuch was first placed over the Beijing and Tong warehouses, and later Huai, Xu, Linqing, and De warehouses also received supervisors, and grain-transport troops and civilians suffered from them.
translations.idiomatic: Granaries initially had no eunuch supervisors; late in Xuande a supervising eunuch was placed over the Beijing and Tong depots, and later Huai'an, Xuzhou, Linqing, and Dezhou depots received them as well, to the harm of transport troops and civilians.

sentences.zh: 世宗用孫交、張孚敬議，撤革諸中官，惟督諸倉者如故。

translations.literal: The Jiajing Emperor, following the proposals of Sun Jiao and Zhang Fuling, removed the various eunuch posts, but those supervising the warehouses remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Jiajing, following Sun Jiao and Zhang Fuling's advice, abolished most eunuch posts but left warehouse supervisors in place.

sentences.zh: 久之，從給事中管懷理言，乃罷之。

translations.literal: After a long time, following Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili, they were finally abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually, at Supervising Secretary Guan Huaili's urging, those posts were abolished as well.

sentences.zh: 初，天下府庫各有存積，邊餉不借支於內，京師不收括於外。

translations.literal: At first every prefectural treasury in the realm had its own reserves; frontier funds were not borrowed from the inner court, and the capital did not sweep up funds from outside.
translations.idiomatic: Initially every prefectural treasury kept its own reserves; frontier funds were not borrowed from the inner court, and the capital did not drain provincial treasuries.

sentences.zh: 成化時，巡鹽御史楊澄始請發各鹽運提舉司贓罰銀入京庫。

translations.literal: In the Chenghua reign Salt-Circuit Censor Yang Cheng first asked to send confiscation and fine silver from each salt transport intendant office to the capital treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Under Chenghua, Salt-Circuit Censor Yang Cheng first proposed sending fine and confiscation silver from salt intendant offices to the capital treasury.

sentences.zh: 弘治時，給事中曾昂請以諸布政司公帑積貯徵徭羨銀，盡輸太倉。

translations.literal: In the Hongzhi reign Supervising Secretary Zeng Ang asked that surplus silver from levies accumulated in the public treasuries of all provincial administration commissions be entirely remitted to Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Hongzhi, Supervising Secretary Zeng Ang proposed remitting all surplus levy silver accumulated in provincial public treasuries to Taicang.

sentences.zh: 尚書周經力爭之，以為有不足者，以識造、賞賚、齋醮、土木之故，必欲盡括天下財，非藏富於民意也。

translations.literal: Minister Zhou Jing argued forcefully that shortfalls arose from commemorative casting, rewards, fasting rites, and construction projects; to want to sweep up all wealth under heaven was not the idea of storing riches among the people.
translations.idiomatic: Minister Zhou Jing argued forcefully that shortfalls came from commemorative casting, rewards, fasting rites, and construction—not from provincial reserves—and that draining every treasury in the realm betrayed the principle of keeping wealth among the people.

sentences.zh: 至劉瑾用事，遂令各省庫藏盡輸京師。

translations.literal: When Liu Jin held power, he ordered every provincial treasury to remit all holdings to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jin seized power, he ordered every provincial treasury to remit all holdings to the capital.

sentences.zh: 世宗時，閩、廣進羨餘，戶部請責他省巡按，歲一奏獻如例。

translations.literal: In the Jiajing reign Fujian and Guangdong presented surplus tribute; the Ministry of Revenue asked that touring censors of other provinces be held responsible to present annual memorial offerings by precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jiajing, Fujian and Guangdong presented surplus tribute; the Ministry of Revenue then required touring censors in every province to submit similar annual offerings.

sentences.zh: 又乙太倉庫匱，運南戶部庫銀八十萬兩實之。

translations.literal: The Taicang treasury vaults were also moved; eight hundred thousand taels of silver from the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue treasury were transported to fill them.
translations.idiomatic: The Taicang vaults were relocated and filled with eight hundred thousand taels transferred from the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue treasury.

sentences.zh: 而戶部條上理財事宜，臨、德二倉積銀二十萬兩，錄以歸太倉。

translations.literal: The Ministry of Revenue also submitted regulations on financial administration: two hundred thousand taels of silver accumulated at the Linqing and De warehouses were recorded and returned to Taicang.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry also submitted fiscal regulations recording two hundred thousand taels accumulated at Linqing and Dezhou and remitted to Taicang.

sentences.zh: 隆慶初，遣四御史分行天下，蒐括庫銀。

translations.literal: Early in Longqing four censors were dispatched across the realm to sweep up treasury silver.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Longqing four censors were sent across the empire to sweep up treasury silver.

sentences.zh: 神宗時，御史蕭重望請核府縣歲額銀進部，未報上。

translations.literal: In the Shenzong reign Censor Xiao Chongwang asked to audit annual silver quotas from prefectures and counties remitted to the ministry; the memorial was not reported upward.
translations.idiomatic: Under Shenzong, Censor Xiao Chongwang proposed auditing annual silver remittances from prefectures and counties to the ministry; the memorial went unanswered.

sentences.zh: 千戶何其賢乞敕內官與己督之，帝竟從其請，由是外儲日就耗。

translations.literal: Thousand-household Officer He Qixian begged an edict for a palace eunuch to supervise with him; the emperor granted the request, and from then on outside reserves daily dwindled.
translations.idiomatic: Thousand-household Officer He Qixian petitioned for a palace eunuch to supervise collections with him; the emperor agreed, and provincial reserves dwindled daily thereafter.

sentences.zh: 至天啟中，用操江巡撫範濟世策，下敕督歲進，收括靡有遺矣。

translations.literal: By the Tianqi reign the policy of Yangtze-defense Grand Coordinator Fan Jishi was adopted; an edict ordered supervision of annual submissions, and collections left nothing behind.
translations.idiomatic: By the Tianqi reign, following Yangtze-defense Grand Coordinator Fan Jishi's plan, an edict ordered supervised annual submissions until nothing remained uncollected.

sentences.zh: 南京內庫頗藏金銀珍寶，魏忠賢矯旨取進，盜竊一空。

translations.literal: The Nanjing inner treasury held considerable gold, silver, and treasures; Wei Zhongxian forged an edict to take them in, and they were stolen clean.
translations.idiomatic: The Nanjing inner treasury held considerable gold, silver, and treasures; Wei Zhongxian forged an edict to seize them, and they were stolen clean.

sentences.zh: 內外匱竭，遂至於亡。

translations.literal: Inner and outer treasuries were exhausted, and the dynasty thus reached its fall.
translations.idiomatic: With inner and outer treasuries exhausted, the dynasty fell.
